definitions.name: Certified translated-dyadic contour bank
definitions.construction:
The certified-real convention is the following.  The integer \(k\) is given exactly, and each of the positive reals \(\delta,\psi_{\eta},R_0,R_1\) is supplied by its canonical nested dyadic enclosure name.  No transform, distribution, oracle, or sample-dependent object is an input.  Put
\[
 R_{\mathrm{fac}}=R_1+1,
 \qquad R_{\mathrm{out}}=R_{\mathrm{fac}}+1,
 \qquad
 Q_{\star}=
 \frac{4\psi_{\eta}^2R_{\mathrm{out}}^2}
      {\log(R_{\mathrm{out}}/R_{\mathrm{fac}})}.
\]
Refine outward intervals until the positive denominator in \(Q_{\star}\) has a positive rational lower endpoint and \(Q_{\star}\) has a finite rational upper endpoint \(U_{\star}\), and set \(N_{\mathrm{cert}}=\lceil U_{\star}\rceil\).  For \(m\ge3\), define
\[
 \mathcal Q_m=
 \{R_0+1/4+q2^{-m}:q\in\mathbb Z,\ 0\le q2^{-m}\le1/2\}.
\]
Let \(m_{\star}\) be the least \(m\ge3\) for which \(|\mathcal Q_m|>N_{\mathrm{cert}}\), enumerate \(\mathcal Q_{m_{\star}}\) increasingly as \(\rho_1<\cdots<\rho_J\), and set
\[
 d_{\star}=2^{-m_{\star}},\qquad h_{\star}=d_{\star}/3,
 \qquad
 \Lambda_{\star}=\frac{R_{\mathrm{fac}}+R_1}{R_{\mathrm{fac}}-R_1},
\]
\[
 a_{\mathrm{an}}=
 \exp\{-4(\Lambda_{\star}-1)\psi_{\eta}^2R_{\mathrm{fac}}^2\}
 \left(\frac{h_{\star}}{R_{\mathrm{fac}}+R_1}\right)^{N_{\mathrm{cert}}}.
\]
Refine an outward interval for \(a_{\mathrm{an}}\) until its rational lower endpoint \(L_{\star}\) is positive.  Let \(u_{\star}\ge1\) be the least integer with \(2^{-u_{\star}}\le L_{\star}\), and set \(a_{\star}=2^{-u_{\star}}\).  Set \(C_j=\{z\in\mathbb C:|z|=\rho_j\}\).  This is the once-for-all translated-dyadic bank.  Its construction inputs are exactly the certified primitive constants \((k,\delta,\psi_{\eta},R_0,R_1)\); the unknown law of \(\eta\) is not an input.  The universal guarantee for treatment-noise transforms is stated and proved separately in \(\text{lem:finite-contour-bank}\).

definitions.name: Canonical certified split-sample statistic on the translated-dyadic bank
definitions.construction:
Use the following canonical representation convention.  For every observed real number \(x\), its input name is the unique nested dyadic name
\[
 \mathcal I_m(x)=
 \left[2^{-m}\lfloor2^m x\rfloor,
       2^{-m}\{\lfloor2^m x\rfloor+1\}\right],
 \qquad m\ge1.
\]
Thus the represented sample consists of the canonical names of \(T_i\), \(Y_i\), and \(\bar g_n(X_i)\), \(1\le i\le n\), together with the canonical certified names of the primitive constants.  The algorithm first invokes \(\text{def:contour-bank-handle}\) internally on \((k,\delta,\psi_{\eta},R_0,R_1)\); it receives no externally chosen bank, contour diagnostics, empirical-transform names, or law-specific information.  It then constructs the canonical interval names of
\[
 Z_{n,i}=T_i-\bar g_n(X_i),
 \qquad
 \widehat F_{a,n}^{(p)}(z)
 =|I_a|^{-1}\sum_{i\in I_a}Z_{n,i}^{p}e^{zZ_{n,i}},
 \quad p\in\{0,1,2\},
\]
and
\[
 \widehat G_{a,n}^{(p)}(z)
 =|I_a|^{-1}\sum_{i\in I_a}Y_iZ_{n,i}^{p}e^{zZ_{n,i}},
 \quad p\in\{0,1\},
\]
by finite outward-rounded rational operations and the standard interval Taylor algorithm for the complex exponential.  In particular, \(\widehat F_{a,n}^{(0)}=\widehat F_{a,n}\) and \(\widehat G_{a,n}^{(0)}=\widehat G_{a,n}\).  These are derived names, not additional inputs.

All contour computations use \(z=\rho_je^{it}\), \(0\le t\le2\pi\), and deterministic uniform angular meshes.  For each fold and circle, the algorithm derives the certified upper bound
\[
 L^F_{aj}=\rho_j\sup_{z\in C_j}|\widehat F_{a,n}'(z)|
 \le \rho_j|I_a|^{-1}\sum_{i\in I_a}|Z_{n,i}|e^{\rho_j|Z_{n,i}|}.
\]
It increases the mesh and the precision of every canonically derived node enclosure until the mesh error is at most \(a_{\star}/128\) and the aggregate node-enclosure error is at most \(a_{\star}/128\).  The minimum of the nodewise rational lower modulus endpoints minus the Lipschitz mesh allowance and the analogous upper endpoint form a canonical certified interval for \(\inf_{C_j}|\widehat F_{a,n}|\) of width at most \(a_{\star}/64\).

Whenever its certified lower endpoint \(m\) is positive, the algorithm derives enclosures of the actual winding integrand
\[
 W_{0j}(t)=
 \rho_je^{it}
 \frac{\widehat F'_{0,n}(\rho_je^{it})}
      {\widehat F_{0,n}(\rho_je^{it})}
\]
and uses the derived sums for \(\widehat F'_{0,n}\) and \(\widehat F''_{0,n}\) to certify
\[
 |W_{0j}'(t)|\le
 \rho_j\frac{\sup_{C_j}|\widehat F'_{0,n}|}{m}
 +\rho_j^2\left\{
 \frac{\sup_{C_j}|\widehat F''_{0,n}|}{m}
 +\frac{\sup_{C_j}|\widehat F'_{0,n}|^2}{m^2}
 \right\}.
\]
It refines the mesh and the canonically derived node enclosures until the outward enclosure of \((2\pi)^{-1}\int_0^{2\pi}W_{0j}(t)\,dt\) has radius strictly below \(1/4\).  If that enclosure contains a unique nonnegative integer, that integer is \(\widehat N_{0j,n}\); otherwise the circle is inadmissible.  Declare \(j\) pilot-admissible when its certified lower modulus endpoint is at least \(a_{\star}/2\) and \(\widehat N_{0j,n}\ge1\).  Let \(\widehat j_n\) be the smallest index among the admissible indices having maximal certified lower modulus endpoint.  Return zero if there is no such index.

On the evaluation fold, compute the same canonical modulus certificate on \(C_{\widehat j_n}\), and return zero if its lower endpoint is below \(a_{\star}/4\).  Otherwise the algorithm derives enclosures of the actual final contour integrand
\[
 V(t)=\rho_{\widehat j_n}e^{it}
 \frac{\widehat G_{1,n}(\rho_{\widehat j_n}e^{it})}
      {\widehat F_{1,n}(\rho_{\widehat j_n}e^{it})}
\]
and the bound
\[
 |V'(t)|\le
 \rho_{\widehat j_n}\frac{\sup|\widehat G_{1,n}|}{m}
 +\rho_{\widehat j_n}^2\left\{
 \frac{\sup|\widehat G'_{1,n}|}{m}
 +\frac{\sup|\widehat G_{1,n}|\sup|\widehat F'_{1,n}|}{m^2}
 \right\}.
\]
It refines until the canonical complex enclosure of
\[
 \frac{1}{2\pi\widehat N_{0\widehat j_n,n}}
 \int_0^{2\pi}V(t)\,dt
\]
has radius at most \(1/n\).  Its canonical rational midpoint is the sole numerical output before taking the real part and projecting onto \([-C_{\theta},C_{\theta}]\); the result is \(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}\).

An execution trace is the finite list of requested name precisions, mesh sizes, rational interval operations, rational comparisons, and branch decisions just described.  All threshold comparisons are comparisons of rational certified endpoints with the fixed rational thresholds, and every division is performed only after a positive rational denominator certificate.  The canonical-name convention makes the trace and output functions of the represented real values, not of arbitrary names.  The definition fixes the thresholds \(a_{\star}/2\) and \(a_{\star}/4\), the fallback zero, the smallest-index tie-break, and the final \(1/n\) error.  It uses \(\bar g_n\), uses no supplied outcome code, and has no access to the law of \(\eta\).  Termination, extensionality, and Borel measurability of this canonical algorithm are conclusions proved in \(\text{thm:adaptive-rootn-minimax}\), not assumptions of the definition.

statements.statement: If \(z_0\) is a zero of \(M\) of multiplicity \(\ell\), then for every real shift \(d\), \(E_P[J_{z_0,\ell}(\eta+d)]=0\). For every \(P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\), this gives \(E_P[J_{z_0,\ell}(Z_n)\mid X]=0\) and \(E_P[Z_nJ_{z_0,\ell}(Z_n)]=M^{(\ell)}(z_0)H_n(z_0)\); whenever this value is nonzero, \(\theta_0=E_P[YJ_{z_0,\ell}(Z_n)]/E_P[Z_nJ_{z_0,\ell}(Z_n)]\).
statements.proof_tex:
\begin{proof}
Fix a zero \(z_0\) of \(M\) having multiplicity \(\ell\).  By the definition of multiplicity,
\[
 M^{(j)}(z_0)=0\quad(0\le j<\ell),
 \qquad M^{(\ell)}(z_0)\ne0.
\]
All differentiations under the expectation below are legitimate: membership in \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\) and \(\text{ass:eta-subgaussian}\), incorporated in \(\text{def:non-gaussian-class}\), give exponential moments of \(\eta\) of every real order, while \(|D_n|\le 2C_g\).  Hence every polynomial times each complex exponential appearing below is integrable, uniformly on compact subsets of the complex plane.

For an arbitrary real number \(d\), the binomial identity and the derivative formula \(M^{(j)}(z)=E_P[\eta^j e^{z\eta}]\) give
\[
\begin{aligned}
 E_P[J_{z_0,\ell}(\eta+d)]
 &=E_P[(\eta+d)^{\ell-1}e^{z_0(\eta+d)}]\\
 &=e^{z_0d}\sum_{j=0}^{\ell-1}
   {\ell-1\choose j}d^{\ell-1-j}E_P[\eta^j e^{z_0\eta}]\\
 &=e^{z_0d}\sum_{j=0}^{\ell-1}
   {\ell-1\choose j}d^{\ell-1-j}M^{(j)}(z_0)=0.
\end{aligned}
\]
This proves the shift-annihilation identity.

Now fix \(P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\).  By \(\text{ass:independent-treatment-noise}\), the conditional law of \(\eta\) given \(X\) equals its marginal law.  Since \(D_n=g_0(X)-\bar g_n(X)\) is \(\sigma(X)\)-measurable and real-valued, the preceding identity, applied conditionally with \(d=D_n\), yields
\[
 E_P[J_{z_0,\ell}(Z_n)\mid X]
 =E_P[J_{z_0,\ell}(\eta+D_n)\mid X]=0
 \quad\text{almost surely}.
\]

Independence also gives the exact transform factorization
\[
 E_P[e^{zZ_n}]
 =E_P[e^{z(\eta+D_n)}]=M(z)H_n(z).
\]
Differentiating this identity \(\ell\) times at \(z_0\), using the product rule and the multiplicity equalities above, gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
 E_P[Z_nJ_{z_0,\ell}(Z_n)]
 &=E_P[Z_n^{\ell}e^{z_0Z_n}]\\
 &=\left.\frac{d^{\ell}}{dz^{\ell}}\{M(z)H_n(z)\}\right|_{z=z_0}\\
 &=\sum_{j=0}^{\ell}{\ell\choose j}
   M^{(j)}(z_0)H_n^{(\ell-j)}(z_0)
 =M^{(\ell)}(z_0)H_n(z_0).
\end{aligned}
\]

Finally, by the displayed residual decomposition,
\[
 Y=\theta_0Z_n+b_n(X)+\xi.
\]
The conditional annihilation identity implies
\[
 E_P[b_n(X)J_{z_0,\ell}(Z_n)]
 =E_P\!\left[b_n(X)E_P[J_{z_0,\ell}(Z_n)\mid X]\right]=0.
\]
Moreover, \(Z_n=T-\bar g_n(X)\), so \(J_{z_0,\ell}(Z_n)\) is \(\sigma(X,T)\)-measurable.  The restriction \(E_P[\xi\mid X,T]=0\) in \(\text{ass:outcome-mean-independence}\) therefore gives
\[
 E_P[\xi J_{z_0,\ell}(Z_n)]
 =E_P\!\left[J_{z_0,\ell}(Z_n)E_P[\xi\mid X,T]\right]=0.
\]
The required products are integrable because \(b_n\) is bounded, \(\xi\) is conditionally sub-Gaussian, \(D_n\) is bounded, and \(\eta\) is sub-Gaussian.  Consequently,
\[
 E_P[YJ_{z_0,\ell}(Z_n)]
 =\theta_0E_P[Z_nJ_{z_0,\ell}(Z_n)].
\]
Whenever the denominator, equivalently \(M^{(\ell)}(z_0)H_n(z_0)\), is nonzero, division is valid and yields
\[
 \theta_0=
 \frac{E_P[YJ_{z_0,\ell}(Z_n)]}
      {E_P[Z_nJ_{z_0,\ell}(Z_n)]}.
\]
\end{proof}
statements.justification: This exact identity displays the global location-family null score and its relevance under residual contamination.
statements.gap: Transform-zero incompleteness is classical, but its multiplicity-adjusted score has not been used to eliminate an arbitrary PLM covariate shift created by a supplied treatment code.
statements.consumer: Known-noise implementations can estimate the causal coefficient by a single bounded or exponentially weighted moment ratio.

statements.statement: For every \(P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\), \(F_n(z)=M(z)H_n(z)\) and \(G_n(z)=\theta_0F_n'(z)+M(z)B_n(z)\) for every \(z\in\mathbb C\).
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\) and \(z\in\mathbb C\).  The sub-Gaussian and boundedness conditions make every expectation and derivative below finite.  Since \(Z_n=\eta+D_n\), \(D_n\) is measurable with respect to \(X\), and \(\eta\perp X\),
\[
 F_n(z)=E_P[e^{z\eta}e^{zD_n}]=M(z)H_n(z).
\]
The residual equation gives \(Y=\theta_0Z_n+b_n(X)+\xi\).  Moreover \(Z_n\) is measurable with respect to \((X,T)\), so outcome mean independence implies
\[
 E_P[\xi e^{zZ_n}]
 =E_P[e^{zZ_n}E_P(\xi\mid X,T)]=0.
\]
Independence again gives
\[
 E_P[b_n(X)e^{zZ_n}]
 =E_P[e^{z\eta}]E_P[b_n(X)e^{zD_n}]=M(z)B_n(z).
\]
Finally, differentiation under the expectation is justified by the same exponential integrability and yields \(F_n'(z)=E_P[Z_ne^{zZ_n}]\).  Substitution proves
\[
 G_n(z)=\theta_0F_n'(z)+M(z)B_n(z).
\]
Both identities hold for every complex \(z\).
statements.justification: The identity recovers the latent transform-zero geometry from observable learned residuals and isolates an analytic nuisance ratio.
statements.gap: Classical convolution results do not provide the outcome transform \(G_n=\theta_0F_n'+MB_n\) for a partially linear causal coefficient.
statements.consumer: The contour theorem integrates \(G_n/F_n\) and removes \(B_n/H_n\) exactly.

statements.statement: For every \(P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\), let \(C_j\) be positively oriented. If \(F_n\) is zero-free on \(C_j\), \(H_n\) is zero-free on and inside \(C_j\), and \(N_{C_j}(F_n)\ge1\), then \(\theta_0=\Theta_{C_j}(F_n,G_n)=\{N_{C_j}(F_n)2\pi i\}^{-1}\oint_{C_j}G_n(z)/F_n(z)\,dz\).
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\).  This membership is the premise needed to invoke \(\text{lem:observable-factorization}\).  On \(C_j\), that lemma and the identity \(F_n=M H_n\) give
\[
 \frac{G_n(z)}{F_n(z)}
 =\theta_0\frac{F_n'(z)}{F_n(z)}+
   \frac{M(z)B_n(z)}{M(z)H_n(z)}
 =\theta_0\frac{F_n'(z)}{F_n(z)}+\frac{B_n(z)}{H_n(z)}.
 \tag{1}
\]
The cancellation in the middle expression is justified pointwise on \(C_j\): by hypothesis \(F_n\) is nonzero there and \(H_n\) is nonzero there, so \(M=F_n/H_n\) is also nonzero there.  Since \(B_n\) and \(H_n\) are entire and \(H_n\) has no zero on or inside \(C_j\), the quotient \(B_n/H_n\) is holomorphic on a neighborhood of the closed disk bounded by \(C_j\).  Cauchy's theorem therefore yields
\[
 \oint_{C_j}\frac{B_n(z)}{H_n(z)}\,dz=0.
 \tag{2}
\]
Because \(F_n\) is entire and zero-free on \(C_j\), the argument principle gives
\[
 \frac{1}{2\pi i}\oint_{C_j}
 \frac{F_n'(z)}{F_n(z)}\,dz=N_{C_j}(F_n).
 \tag{3}
\]
Integrating (1) and using (2)--(3) gives
\[
 \frac{1}{2\pi i}\oint_{C_j}\frac{G_n(z)}{F_n(z)}\,dz
 =\theta_0N_{C_j}(F_n).
 \tag{4}
\]
The assumed count is a positive integer, so division by \(N_{C_j}(F_n)\) is valid.  Applying \(\text{def:contour-functional}\) to (4) proves
\[
 \theta_0
 =\Theta_{C_j}(F_n,G_n)
 =\frac{1}{N_{C_j}(F_n)2\pi i}
   \oint_{C_j}\frac{G_n(z)}{F_n(z)}\,dz.
\]
Thus the causal target remains \(\theta_0(P)\), while the displayed observable contour ratio is its identifying functional only for a law in the stated class and under the stated boundary, zero-free, and positive-count conditions.
statements.justification: For a law \(P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\), the learned-residual factorization makes the observable contour formula identify the coefficient without an outcome regression once a valid contour is given.
statements.gap: The identity requires class membership as well as the boundary zero-free, nuisance-transform zero-free, and positive-count conditions; it neither constructs nor computes the uniformly conditioned contour bank.
statements.consumer: The certified estimator fixes \(P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\) and evaluates this population identity on its selected translated-dyadic contour.

statements.statement:
With the exact Luxemburg convention in \(\text{ass:eta-subgaussian}\), set
\[
 A_k=(2^{k+4}k!)^{1/(k-2)},
 \qquad
 R_0=A_k(\psi_{\eta}^2/\delta)^{1/(k-2)}.
\]
Every centered law satisfying \(\|\eta\|_{\psi_2}\le\psi_{\eta}\) and \(|\kappa_k(\eta)|\ge\delta\) has a zero of \(M\) in \(\{z\in\mathbb C:|z|\le R_0\}\). Thus the zero-localization radius is the displayed numerical function of the primitive constants.
statements.proof_tex:
Write \(\psi=\psi_{\eta}\).  The exact Luxemburg premise gives
\[
 E_P\exp(\eta^2/\psi^2)\le2,
 \qquad E_P\eta=0.
\]
We first derive a numerical growth bound.  Let \(\eta'\) be an independent copy of \(\eta\).  If \(|t|\psi\le1\), Jensen's inequality and centering give
\[
 E_Pe^{t\eta}\le E_Pe^{t(\eta-\eta')}.
\]
The difference \(\eta-\eta'\) is symmetric.  Using \(\cosh u\le e^{u^2/2}\), \((\eta-\eta')^2\le2\eta^2+2(\eta')^2\), and then the Lyapunov inequality with exponent \(t^2\psi^2\le1\), we obtain
\[
\begin{aligned}
 E_Pe^{t\eta}
 &\le E_P\cosh\{t(\eta-\eta')\}\\
 &\le E_P\exp\{t^2(\eta-\eta')^2/2\}\\
 &\le \{E_Pe^{t^2\eta^2}\}^2
 \le 2^{2t^2\psi^2}
 \le e^{4\psi^2t^2}.
\end{aligned}
\]
If \(|t|\psi>1\), Young's inequality and Cauchy--Schwarz yield
\[
 t\eta\le\frac{\eta^2}{2\psi^2}+\frac{t^2\psi^2}{2},
 \qquad
 E_Pe^{t\eta}\le\sqrt2\,e^{t^2\psi^2/2}
 \le e^{4\psi^2t^2}.
\]
Consequently, for every \(z\in\mathbb C\),
\[
 |M(z)|\le E_Pe^{\operatorname{Re}(z)\eta}
 \le \exp(4\psi^2|z|^2). \tag{1}
\]

Suppose for contradiction that \(M\) has no zero in the closed disk of radius \(R_0\).  Since \(M(0)=1\), an analytic logarithm \(f=\log M\), normalized by \(f(0)=0\), exists on a neighborhood of that disk.  Centering gives \(f'(0)=0\).  For \(0<R<R_0\), (1) gives
\[
 \sup_{|z|\le R}\operatorname{Re}f(z)\le4\psi^2R^2.
\]
Apply the Carath\'eodory coefficient estimate on the radius-\(R\) disk to the positive-real-part analytic function \(4\psi^2R^2-f\).  Its value at zero is \(4\psi^2R^2\), and hence
\[
 |f^{(k)}(0)|
 \le 2k!R^{-k}\,4\psi^2R^2
 =8k!\psi^2R^{2-k}. \tag{2}
\]
Letting \(R\uparrow R_0\), using \(f^{(k)}(0)=\kappa_k(\eta)\), and invoking \(\text{ass:cumulant-separation}\), we get
\[
 \delta\le8k!\psi^2R_0^{2-k}.
\]
But the displayed definitions of \(A_k\) and \(R_0\) give
\[
 8k!\psi^2R_0^{2-k}
 =\frac{8k!}{2^{k+4}k!}\,\delta
 =2^{-k-1}\delta<\delta,
\]
a contradiction.  Thus \(M\) has a zero in \(\{|z|\le R_0\}\), with the asserted numerical radius.
statements.justification: The exact Luxemburg normalization yields the displayed numerical radius rather than an unspecified universal constant.
statements.gap: The result localizes a transform zero but does not by itself provide boundary conditioning.
statements.consumer: The certified translated-dyadic bank is built outside this explicit disk.

statements.statement:
Under the certified-real input convention of \(\text{def:contour-bank-handle}\), its terminating finite searches compute, from the displayed primitive class constants and without access to the unknown law of \(\eta\), a finite translated-dyadic bank \(C_j=\{z:|z|=\rho_j\}\), \(1\le j\le J\), with \(R_0<\rho_j<R_1\), and a positive dyadic rational \(a_{\star}\). Every treatment-noise transform represented in \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\) has some \(j\) such that \(N_{C_j}(M)\ge1\) and
\[
 \inf_{z\in C_j}|M(z)|\ge a_{\star}.
\]
The same computed bank and certificate work uniformly in \(n\).
statements.proof_tex:
Fix a treatment-noise transform \(M\) represented in \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\).  By \(\text{lem:zero-localization}\), it has a zero in \(\{|z|\le R_0\}\), so every bank circle encloses at least one zero.  The transform bound proved in that lemma gives, for every \(z\in\mathbb C\),
\[
 |M(z)|\le \exp(4\psi_{\eta}^2|z|^2). \tag{1}
\]

We first audit the zero count used by the finite search.  Let \(s\in(R_{\mathrm{fac}},R_{\mathrm{out}})\) be a radius on which \(M\) has no zero.  Factoring the finitely many zeros in \(\{|z|<s\}\), using
\[
 \frac1{2\pi}\int_0^{2\pi}\log|se^{it}-a|\,dt=\log s
 \quad (|a|<s),
\]
and applying the mean-value identity to the logarithm of the modulus of the remaining zero-free factor gives
\[
 \sum_{|a|<s}\log\frac{s}{|a|}
 =\frac1{2\pi}\int_0^{2\pi}\log|M(se^{it})|\,dt-log|M(0)|.
\]
Here zeros are repeated according to multiplicity and \(M(0)=1\).  Every zero with \(|a|<R_{\mathrm{fac}}\) contributes at least \(\log(s/R_{\mathrm{fac}})\).  By (1), if \(N\) is the number of those zeros, then
\[
 N\log\frac{s}{R_{\mathrm{fac}}}
 \le4\psi_{\eta}^2s^2.
\]
Letting such radii \(s\) increase to \(R_{\mathrm{out}}\) yields
\[
 N\le
 Q_{\star}:=
 \frac{4\psi_{\eta}^2R_{\mathrm{out}}^2}
      {\log(R_{\mathrm{out}}/R_{\mathrm{fac}})}
 \le N_{\mathrm{cert}}. \tag{2}
\]

The grid \(\mathcal Q_{m_{\star}}\) is finite, lies in \((R_0,R_1)\), has more than \(N_{\mathrm{cert}}\) points, and has spacing \(d_{\star}\).  Since \(2h_{\star}=2d_{\star}/3<d_{\star}\), the modulus of a fixed zero can lie at distance less than \(h_{\star}\) from at most one grid point.  Any zero that can violate this separation satisfies \(|a|<R_1+h_{\star}<R_{\mathrm{fac}}\), so it is among the at most \(N_{\mathrm{cert}}\) zeros counted in (2).  The pigeonhole principle therefore supplies a grid radius \(\rho_j\) such that
\[
 \bigl||a|-\rho_j\bigr|\ge h_{\star} \tag{3}
\]
for every zero \(a\) strictly inside the disk of radius \(R_{\mathrm{fac}}\).  In particular, \(M\) is zero-free on \(C_j\).  Because \(\rho_j>R_0\), that circle encloses the zero localized in \(\{|z|\le R_0\}\), and hence \(N_{C_j}(M)\ge1\).

Let \(a_1,\ldots,a_N\), repeated according to multiplicity, be precisely the zeros strictly inside the disk of radius \(R_{\mathrm{fac}}\), and form the disk Blaschke product
\[
 Q(z)=\prod_{\nu=1}^N
 \frac{R_{\mathrm{fac}}(z-a_\nu)}
      {R_{\mathrm{fac}}^2-\overline{a_\nu}z}.
\]
Set \(f=M/Q\), filling the removable singularities.  The function \(f\) is holomorphic and zero-free on the open disk of radius \(R_{\mathrm{fac}}\).  On its boundary, every displayed factor has modulus one, so \(|f|=|M|\).  Cauchy's integral formula applied to \(f^m\), followed by taking the \(m\)-th root and letting \(m\to\infty\), gives from (1)
\[
 |f(z)|\le \exp(4\psi_{\eta}^2R_{\mathrm{fac}}^2),
 \qquad |z|<R_{\mathrm{fac}}. \tag{4}
\]
Moreover, \(|Q(0)|\le1\) and \(M(0)=1\), whence \(|f(0)|\ge1\).

Put \(A=4\psi_{\eta}^2R_{\mathrm{fac}}^2\) and \(u=A-\log|f|\).  By (4), \(u\) is a nonnegative harmonic function and \(u(0)\le A\).  To make the required interior bound explicit, apply the Poisson formula on a circle of radius \(s\in(R_1,R_{\mathrm{fac}})\).  Its kernel is at most \((s+|z|)/(s-|z|)\), while the mean-value identity makes the average boundary value equal to \(u(0)\).  Thus
\[
 u(z)\le\frac{s+|z|}{s-|z|}u(0).
\]
Letting \(s\uparrow R_{\mathrm{fac}}\) and using \(|z|\le R_1\) yields
\[
 u(z)\le\Lambda_{\star}A,
 \qquad
 |f(z)|\ge
 \exp\{-4(\Lambda_{\star}-1)\psi_{\eta}^2R_{\mathrm{fac}}^2\}. \tag{5}
\]
For \(z\in C_j\), (3) implies for every disk factor
\[
 \left|
 \frac{R_{\mathrm{fac}}(z-a_\nu)}
      {R_{\mathrm{fac}}^2-\overline{a_\nu}z}
 \right|
 \ge \frac{|z-a_\nu|}{R_{\mathrm{fac}}+|z|}
 \ge \frac{h_{\star}}{R_{\mathrm{fac}}+R_1}.
\]
The last base belongs to \((0,1)\), and \(N\le N_{\mathrm{cert}}\).  Multiplication and (5) therefore give
\[
 \inf_{z\in C_j}|M(z)|
 \ge
 \exp\{-4(\Lambda_{\star}-1)\psi_{\eta}^2R_{\mathrm{fac}}^2\}
 \left(\frac{h_{\star}}{R_{\mathrm{fac}}+R_1}\right)^{N_{\mathrm{cert}}}
 =a_{\mathrm{an}}
 \ge a_{\star}>0. \tag{6}
\]

It remains to verify effectiveness.  The canonical certified names of \((k,\delta,\psi_{\eta},R_0,R_1)\) give outward rational intervals for every displayed arithmetic expression.  Since \(\log(R_{\mathrm{out}}/R_{\mathrm{fac}})>0\), refinement eventually gives that denominator a positive rational lower endpoint and gives \(Q_{\star}\) a finite rational upper endpoint \(U_{\star}\).  Hence \(N_{\mathrm{cert}}=\lceil U_{\star}\rceil\) is computed after finitely many operations.  The search for \(m_{\star}\) and enumeration of its finite grid terminate.  Since \(a_{\mathrm{an}}>0\), refinement eventually supplies a positive rational lower endpoint \(L_{\star}\); the integer search for the least \(u_{\star}\ge1\) with \(2^{-u_{\star}}\le L_{\star}\) also terminates and returns the prescribed positive dyadic rational \(a_{\star}\).  No operation queries \(M\), \(\eta\), or their law.  Equations (1)--(6) apply to every represented transform and contain no \(n\)-dependent choice, proving the uniform claim.
statements.justification: The translated-dyadic search and Blaschke--Harnack bound compute one uniformly conditioned bank from certified-real primitive constants without the unknown noise law.
statements.gap: Its certificate deteriorates with the fixed separation constants and does not resolve shrinking separation.
statements.consumer: The certified selector uses the bank and dyadic modulus in every stopping rule.

statements.statement:
If \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\neq\varnothing\), then it contains a one-dimensional submodel \(\{P_{n,\vartheta}:|\vartheta|\le c_0\}\) with the same law of \((X,T)\), the same \(g_0,q_0,\bar g_n,\bar q_n\), independent Gaussian outcome innovation of fixed positive variance not exceeding the \(\psi_{\xi}\) envelope, and \(Y_{\vartheta}=q_0(X)+\vartheta\eta+\xi_{\star}\). For \(|\vartheta_1-\vartheta_0|=h/\sqrt n\), \(D_{\mathrm{KL}}(P_{n,\vartheta_0}^{\otimes n}\|P_{n,\vartheta_1}^{\otimes n})\le C_0h^2\), where \(c_0,C_0\) depend only on fixed class constants. Moreover, whenever \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\neq\varnothing\), the same construction may be started from any \(P^{\circ}\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) and preserves its law of \((X,T)\), the functions \(g_0,q_0\), the noise \(\eta\), both clipped supplied codes, and therefore the two bounds
\[
 \|\bar g_n-g_0\|_{L^r(P_X)}\le\varepsilon_{1,n},
 \qquad
 \|\bar q_n-q_0\|_{L^r(P_X)}\le\varepsilon_{2,n}.
\]
Every law on this second path belongs to \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\), has target \(\theta_0(P_{n,\vartheta})=\vartheta\), and obeys the same product relative-entropy bound. Consequently there is \(c_{\mathrm{ACE}}>0\), depending only on the fixed class constants, such that for every \(n\ge2\) with \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\neq\varnothing\),
\[
 \inf_{\widetilde\theta(O_1,\ldots,O_n;\bar g_n,\bar q_n)}
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}}
 E_P[(\widetilde\theta-\theta_0(P))^2]
 \ge \frac{c_{\mathrm{ACE}}}{n}.
\]
statements.proof_tex:
Fix
\[
 \tau=\frac{\psi_{\xi}}4>0,
 \qquad
 c_0=\min\{C_{\theta},1\}>0,
\]
and let \(\xi_{\star}\sim N(0,\tau^2)\) be independent of \((X,T)\). For the exact Luxemburg convention, if \(W\sim N(0,\tau^2)\), then
\[
 E\exp(W^2/u^2)=(1-2\tau^2/u^2)^{-1/2}
 \quad\text{for }u^2>2\tau^2.
\]
It follows that \(\|W\|_{\psi_2}=\sqrt{8/3}\,\tau<\psi_{\xi}\). Thus the chosen innovation has fixed positive variance and satisfies the required conditional sub-Gaussian envelope when conditioned on any \(X\).

First suppose \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\neq\varnothing\) and fix \(P^{\circ}\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\). Preserve its joint law of \((X,T)\), hence its \(g_0\), \(\eta=T-g_0(X)\), covariate law, deterministic clipped codes, and code errors. Preserve also its function \(q_0\), and, for \(|\vartheta|\le c_0\), define
\[
 Y_{\vartheta}=q_0(X)+\vartheta\eta+\xi_{\star}.
 \tag{1}
\]
Since \(\eta\perp X\) and \(E\eta=0\),
\[
 E[Y_{\vartheta}\mid X]=q_0(X).
\]
The residual innovation under coefficient \(\vartheta\) is exactly \(\xi_{\star}\), and independence gives
\[
 E[\xi_{\star}\mid X,T]=0.
\]
The target range holds because \(|\vartheta|\le c_0\le C_{\theta}\). The bounds on \(g_0\) and \(q_0\), independence and sub-Gaussianity of \(\eta\), its cumulant separation, and the direct \(L^1(P_X)\) treatment-code bound are unchanged. The displayed Gaussian calculation gives the conditional sub-Gaussian bound for the new outcome innovation. Hence every law \(P_{n,\vartheta}\) defined by (1) belongs to \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\), and all objects asserted to be common along the path are indeed common.

Conditional on \((X,T)\), two path laws differ only in the means of normal distributions with common variance \(\tau^2\). Therefore
\[
 D_{\mathrm{KL}}(P_{n,\vartheta_0}\|P_{n,\vartheta_1})
 =\frac{(\vartheta_1-\vartheta_0)^2}{2\tau^2}E[(T-g_0(X))^2]
 =\frac{(\vartheta_1-\vartheta_0)^2}{2\tau^2}E[\eta^2].
 \tag{2}
\]
The exact treatment-noise Luxemburg condition and Jensen's inequality imply
\[
 \exp\{E\eta^2/\psi_{\eta}^2\}
 \le E\exp(\eta^2/\psi_{\eta}^2)\le2,
 \qquad
 E\eta^2\le\psi_{\eta}^2\log2.
 \tag{3}
\]
Additivity of relative entropy for independent products, (2), and (3) show that whenever \(|\vartheta_1-\vartheta_0|=h/\sqrt n\),
\[
 D_{\mathrm{KL}}(P_{n,\vartheta_0}^{\otimes n}\|P_{n,\vartheta_1}^{\otimes n})
 \le C_0h^2,
 \qquad
 C_0=\frac{\psi_{\eta}^2\log2}{2\tau^2}.
 \tag{4}
\]
This proves the first branch with constants depending only on the fixed class constants.

Now suppose \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\neq\varnothing\) and fix an arbitrary \(P^{\circ}\) in that class. Repeat (1), preserving the joint law of \((X,T)\), the functions \(g_0,q_0\), the treatment noise \(\eta\), and the deterministic functions \(\bar g_n,\bar q_n\). We verify every condition in \(\text{def:jms-ace-class}\). The restrictions on \(g_0\) and \(q_0\) are unchanged. All treatment-side properties are unchanged: \(\eta\perp X\), \(\|\eta\|_{\psi_2}\le\psi_{\eta}\), and \(|\kappa_{r+1}(\eta)|\ge\delta\). Because neither regression function nor either clipped code changes,
\[
 \|\bar g_n-g_0\|_{L^r(P_X)}\le\varepsilon_{1,n},
 \qquad
 \|\bar q_n-q_0\|_{L^r(P_X)}\le\varepsilon_{2,n}
\]
remain exactly the original two inequalities. The new coefficient obeys \(|\vartheta|\le c_0\le C_{\theta}\). The new residual is \(\xi_{\star}\), so the calculation above gives \(\|\xi_{\star}\|_{\psi_2\mid X}\le\psi_{\xi}\) almost surely, and independence gives \(E[\xi_{\star}\mid X,T]=0\). Finally, the size-\(n\) experiment is the independent product \(P_{n,\vartheta}^{\otimes n}\), exactly as required by \(\text{ass:iid-sampling}\). Thus every law on the second path belongs to \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\), and (2)--(4) apply without change.

It remains to turn this path into the asserted ACE-class converse. Choose
\[
 0<h\le\min\{c_0,1,(8C_0)^{-1/2}\},
 \qquad
 \vartheta_{\pm}=\pm\frac{h}{2\sqrt n}.
\]
For every \(n\ge2\), both values lie in the path, their separation is \(h/\sqrt n\), and (4) gives product relative entropy at most \(1/8\). Pinsker's inequality, which follows from the binary log-sum bound, gives
\[
 \|P_{n,\vartheta_-}^{\otimes n}-P_{n,\vartheta_+}^{\otimes n}\|_{\mathrm{TV}}
 \le\sqrt{\frac12D_{\mathrm{KL}}(P_{n,\vartheta_-}^{\otimes n}\|P_{n,\vartheta_+}^{\otimes n})}
 \le\frac14.
 \tag{5}
\]
For an arbitrary estimator \(\widetilde\theta\), put \(A=\{\widetilde\theta\ge0\}\). On \(A\) under the negative law, or on \(A^c\) under the positive law, the squared error is at least \(h^2/(4n)\). Hence
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \max_{v\in\{-,+\}}
 E_{P_{n,\vartheta_v}}[(\widetilde\theta-\vartheta_v)^2]
 &\ge \frac{h^2}{8n}
 \{P_{n,\vartheta_-}^{\otimes n}(A)
   +P_{n,\vartheta_+}^{\otimes n}(A^c)\}\\
 &\ge \frac{h^2}{8n}
 \{1-\|P_{n,\vartheta_-}^{\otimes n}-P_{n,\vartheta_+}^{\otimes n}\|_{\mathrm{TV}}\}\\
 &\ge\frac{3h^2}{32n}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Both laws belong to the published ACE class. Taking the supremum over that class and then the infimum over all sample estimators proves the final display with \(c_{\mathrm{ACE}}=3h^2/32>0\).
statements.justification: The lower bound uses an explicit Gaussian-outcome-innovation path that preserves the law of \(X,T\), both regression functions, and the deterministic supplied codes.
statements.gap: A generic appeal to a parametric submodel would not verify membership in the triangular common-code class or the conditional sub-Gaussian innovation envelope.
statements.consumer: The self-contained two-point KL argument converts this path into the \(c/n\) minimax lower bound.

statements.statement:
Under the certified-real input convention, \(\text{def:contour-bank-handle}\) and \(\text{lem:finite-contour-bank}\) compute once for all a deterministic translated-dyadic bank and a positive dyadic rational \(a_{\star}\) from the displayed primitive class constants, without access to the unknown law of \(\eta\). There are constants \(0<c<C<\infty\), depending only on \(r,\delta,C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\eta},\psi_{\xi}\), such that the associated total measurable certified statistic \(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}\) in \(\text{def:adaptive-contour-estimator}\) satisfies, for every \(n\ge2\) with \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\neq\varnothing\) and \(\varepsilon_{1,n}\le\varepsilon_0\),
\[
 \frac cn\le\mathfrak R_n^{\mathrm{NG}}
 \le\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}}
 E_P[(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}-\theta_0(P))^2]
 \le\frac Cn.
\]
The statistic is a computable observed-sample map from the supplied certified-real names, uses \(\bar g_n\), uses no supplied outcome code, and does not know the law of \(\eta\). Its MSE bound implies
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}}
 Q_{P,1-\gamma}(|\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}-\theta_0(P)|)
 \le\sqrt{C/(\gamma n)}.
\]
Moreover, \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\subseteq\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\). Hence, whenever \(n\ge2\), \(\varepsilon_{1,n}\le\varepsilon_0\), and \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\neq\varnothing\),
\[
 \frac cn
 \le
 \inf_{\widetilde\theta(O_1,\ldots,O_n;\bar g_n,\bar q_n)}
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}}
 E_P[(\widetilde\theta-\theta_0(P))^2]
 \le
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}}
 E_P[(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}-\theta_0(P))^2]
 \le\frac Cn,
\]
and
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}}
 Q_{P,1-\gamma}(|\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}-\theta_0(P)|)
 \le\sqrt{C/(\gamma n)}.
\]
No inclusion \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\subseteq\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) is asserted. The finite-order ACE and spectral generalized-quantile guarantees may therefore be compared on the full published ACE class, and that class itself has matched \(\Theta(n^{-1})\) minimax mean-squared error. The latter lower bound is over all estimators on the class; it is not a lower bound on \(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{ACE},r,n}\) or on its cited generalized-quantile guarantee. The class \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}^{\mathrm{ACE}}\) remains the additional \(L^s(P_X)\)-restricted subclass and equals the published ACE class when \(s=r\) under the common clipped-code convention. The constants may deteriorate with fixed \(\delta\), and this theorem gives no useful shrinking-\(\delta_n\) rate, adaptive switching rule, uniform inference result, or matching local lower bound.
statements.proof_tex:
We separate the computation audit, the broad-class upper bound, the two converses, and the comparator scope.

\emph{Canonical computation.} The bank algorithm in \(\text{def:contour-bank-handle}\) terminates by \(\text{lem:finite-contour-bank}\) and uses only the canonical certified names of \((k,\delta,\psi_{\eta},R_0,R_1)\). Given the represented sample, subtraction, multiplication, absolute value, and the interval Taylor algorithm for the exponential convert the canonical dyadic names of \(T_i,Y_i,\bar g_n(X_i)\) into outward rational enclosures for every finite sum defining \(\widehat F_{a,n}^{(p)}\) and \(\widehat G_{a,n}^{(p)}\). Refinement makes every such enclosure arbitrarily narrow.

For a fixed circle, the derived bound \(L^F_{aj}\) is finite. Hence a finite uniform mesh makes its Lipschitz allowance at most \(a_{\star}/128\), and finite refinement makes the aggregate node error at most \(a_{\star}/128\). Thus every modulus certificate terminates. A winding computation is attempted only after a positive rational denominator certificate has been obtained. The displayed derivative bound for \(W_{0j}\) is then finite, so finite mesh and precision refinement produce an enclosure of radius below \(1/4\). Because \(\widehat F_{0,n}(0)=1\), the empirical entire function is not identically zero. Its zeros inside a zero-free bank circle are isolated and finite, and the logarithmic-derivative integral equals their nonnegative integer count. Therefore the radius-below-\(1/4\) enclosure contains a unique nonnegative integer. The finite bank, rational comparisons, and prescribed smallest-index tie-break make pilot selection terminate. The same argument applies to the evaluation modulus. If that certificate passes, the derivative bound for \(V\) is finite, so finite refinement reaches the required radius \(1/n\). Every branch therefore returns either the prescribed fallback or one rational midpoint after finitely many operations.

The dyadic name \(\mathcal I_m(x)\) is uniquely determined by \(x\). Equal primitive constants and equal represented sample values consequently generate the same interval queries, rational trace, and output, so the algorithm is extensional. For Borel measurability, fix a finite trace. Each queried endpoint is a floor of a scaled sample coordinate and hence is Borel; \(\bar g_n(X_i)\) is Borel because \(\bar g_n\) is measurable. Finite interval operations and rational branch comparisons preserve Borel dependence. There are countably many finite traces, and the output on each terminal trace is a Borel rational expression followed by real part and continuous projection. The countable union over terminal traces proves that \(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}\) is a total Borel measurable observed-sample map. It uses \(\bar g_n\), no supplied outcome code, and no treatment-noise law.

\emph{Uniform upper bound.} Put \(m_a=|I_a|\). For \(n\ge2\), \(m_a\ge n/3\). Fix \(P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\), and choose \(j_{\star}\) from \(\text{lem:finite-contour-bank}\). By \(\text{lem:l1-nuisance-zero-free}\),
\[
 N_{C_{j_{\star}}}(F_n)\ge1,
 \qquad
 \inf_{C_{j_{\star}}}|F_n|\ge\frac{3a_{\star}}4.
 \tag{1}
\]
Define
\[
 d_a=\sup_{|z|\le R_1}|\widehat F_{a,n}(z)-F_n(z)|,
 \qquad
 e_a=\sup_{|z|\le R_1}|\widehat G_{a,n}(z)-G_n(z)|,
 \qquad
 \mathcal A_a=\{d_a\le a_{\star}/8\}.
\]
On \(\mathcal A_0\), the canonical modulus interval for \(j_{\star}\), whose width is at most \(a_{\star}/64\), has lower endpoint at least
\[
 \left(\frac34-\frac18-\frac1{64}\right)a_{\star}
 =\frac{39}{64}a_{\star}.
 \tag{2}
\]
The straight-line homotopy from \(F_n\) to \(\widehat F_{0,n}\) is nonzero on \(C_{j_{\star}}\), so the empirical and population winding counts coincide and are positive. Thus \(j_{\star}\) is pilot-admissible.

Let \(C=C_{\widehat j_n}\). Maximality of the selected certified lower endpoint and (2), followed by subtraction of \(d_0\), imply
\[
 \inf_C|F_n|
 \ge\left(\frac{39}{64}-\frac18\right)a_{\star}
 =\frac{31}{64}a_{\star}.
 \tag{3}
\]
The same homotopy argument on the selected circle gives
\[
 \widehat N_{0\widehat j_n,n}=N_C(F_n)=:N\ge1.
 \tag{4}
\]
On \(\mathcal A_0\cap\mathcal A_1\), (3) gives an evaluation empirical modulus of at least \(23a_{\star}/64\). Subtracting the enclosure width gives the certified lower endpoint
\[
 \frac{22}{64}a_{\star}>\frac14a_{\star}.
 \tag{5}
\]
Thus no fallback occurs on this event.

There is a finite class-uniform constant \(C_G\) such that
\[
 \sup_{|z|\le R_1}|G_n(z)|\le C_G.
 \tag{6}
\]
Indeed, \(|D_n|\le2C_g\), \(Z_n=\eta+D_n\), and \(Y=q_0(X)+\theta_0\eta+\xi\). The exact Luxemburg inequality gives
\[
 E e^{t|\eta|}\le\sqrt2\exp(t^2\psi_{\eta}^2/2),
\]
by \(t|\eta|\le\eta^2/(2\psi_{\eta}^2)+t^2\psi_{\eta}^2/2\). It also gives uniform second moments for \(\eta\) and \(\xi\). Cauchy--Schwarz therefore bounds \(E[|Y|e^{R_1|Z_n|}]\) using only \(C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\eta},\psi_{\xi}\), and \(R_1\), proving (6) without requiring independence between \(\xi\) and \(\eta\).

On \(\mathcal A_0\cap\mathcal A_1\), subtract the empirical and population ratios on \(C\). Equations (3), (5), and (6), together with \(\operatorname{len}(C)\le2\pi R_1\) and \(N\ge1\), give
\[
 \left|
 \frac{1}{N2\pi i}\oint_C
 \frac{\widehat G_{1,n}(z)}{\widehat F_{1,n}(z)}\,dz
 -
 \frac{1}{N2\pi i}\oint_C
 \frac{G_n(z)}{F_n(z)}\,dz
 \right|
 \le L_{\star}(d_1+e_1),
 \tag{7}
\]
where, with \(\mu=31a_{\star}/64\) and \(\nu=23a_{\star}/64\), one may take
\[
 L_{\star}=R_1\max\{\nu^{-1},C_G(\mu\nu)^{-1}\}.
\]
The hypotheses of \(\text{thm:exact-contour-identification}\) hold: (3) makes \(F_n\) zero-free on \(C\), \(\text{lem:l1-nuisance-zero-free}\) makes \(H_n\) zero-free on and inside \(C\), and (4) gives the positive zero count. Hence the second contour functional in (7) equals the causal target \(\theta_0\). The certified midpoint adds complex error at most \(1/n\); taking its real part and projecting onto \([-C_{\theta},C_{\theta}]\) cannot increase its distance from \(\theta_0\).

By \(\text{lem:empirical-transform-uniform-l2}\), uniformly in \(P\),
\[
 E_P(d_a^2+e_a^2)\le\frac{3K}{n},
 \qquad
 P(\mathcal A_0^c\cup\mathcal A_1^c)
 \le\frac{384K}{a_{\star}^2n}.
 \tag{8}
\]
On the exceptional event, projection bounds squared error by \(4C_{\theta}^2\). On the good event, (7), \((d_1+e_1)^2\le2(d_1^2+e_1^2)\), and the numerical error contribute at most \(12L_{\star}^2K/n+2/n^2\) in expectation. Consequently
\[
 C_{\mathrm{up}}
 =12L_{\star}^2K
 +\frac{1536C_{\theta}^2K}{a_{\star}^2}+2
\]
is valid, and
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}}
 E_P[(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}-\theta_0(P))^2]
 \le\frac{C_{\mathrm{up}}}{n}.
 \tag{9}
\]
The bank, \(a_{\star}\), \(C_G\), \(K\), and \(L_{\star}\) depend only on the displayed fixed class constants. The statistic is therefore one admissible data-driven minimax rule, proving \(\mathfrak R_n^{\mathrm{NG}}\le C_{\mathrm{up}}/n\).

\emph{Broad-class converse.} Invoke the first branch of \(\text{lem:non-gaussian-hard-submodel}\). Choose fixed \(h>0\), depending only on the class constants, small enough that \(\vartheta_{\pm}=\pm h/(2\sqrt n)\) belong to the path for every \(n\ge2\) and
\[
 D_{\mathrm{KL}}(P_-^{\otimes n}\|P_+^{\otimes n})\le\frac18.
\]
Pinsker's inequality gives total variation at most \(1/4\). Testing by the sign of an arbitrary estimator yields
\[
 \max_{v\in\{-,+\}}
 E_{P_{n,\vartheta_v}}[(\widetilde\theta-\vartheta_v)^2]
 \ge\frac{h^2}{8n}
 \{1-\|P_-^{\otimes n}-P_+^{\otimes n}\|_{\mathrm{TV}}\}
 \ge\frac{3h^2}{32n}.
\]
Taking the class supremum and estimator infimum proves \(c_{\mathrm{NG}}/n\le\mathfrak R_n^{\mathrm{NG}}\), with \(c_{\mathrm{NG}}=3h^2/32\).

\emph{Published ACE-class converse and upper bound.} By \(\text{lem:jms-ace-class-relations}\),
\[
 \mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}
 \subseteq\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}.
 \tag{10}
\]
When the published class is nonempty and \(\varepsilon_{1,n}\le\varepsilon_0\), restriction of (9) to (10) gives
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}}
 E_P[(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}-\theta_0(P))^2]
 \le\frac{C_{\mathrm{up}}}{n}.
 \tag{11}
\]
The second branch of \(\text{lem:non-gaussian-hard-submodel}\) gives, on this same class,
\[
 \inf_{\widetilde\theta(O_1,\ldots,O_n;\bar g_n,\bar q_n)}
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}}
 E_P[(\widetilde\theta-\theta_0(P))^2]
 \ge\frac{c_{\mathrm{ACE}}}{n}.
 \tag{12}
\]
The middle inequality in the claimed ACE bracket is simply the definition of an infimum: the certified statistic is one admissible estimator. Set
\[
 c=\min\{c_{\mathrm{NG}},c_{\mathrm{ACE}}\}>0,
 \qquad
 C=C_{\mathrm{up}}.
\]
Equations (9), (11), and (12) prove both matched minimax MSE brackets with the same displayed constants.

Finally, Markov's inequality applied to (9) gives
\[
 P\!\left(
 |\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}-\theta_0(P)|
 >\sqrt{C/(\gamma n)}
 \right)\le\gamma,
\]
which is the broad-class generalized-quantile bound; restriction through (10) proves the full published ACE-class version. The same class-relation lemma proves the stated relation with \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}^{\mathrm{ACE}}\), while it gives no reverse inclusion of the broad spectral class in the published ACE class.

The lower bound in (12) concerns the minimax MSE over all estimators on the published class. It says nothing about the risk of the particular ACE estimator and does not turn the cited generalized-quantile upper bound into a lower bound. Thus the ACE-versus-spectral generalized-quantile comparison remains upper-versus-upper. All computed constants are fixed only for fixed \(\delta>0\); no shrinking-separation rate, adaptive selector, uniform inference result, or matching local lower bound follows.
statements.justification: The total certified statistic attains a matched parametric MSE rate for the scalar causal coefficient without an outcome learner or knowledge of the treatment-noise law.
statements.gap: The constants are fixed-separation constants and do not yield a useful shrinking-separation rate or uniform inference theorem.
statements.consumer: Use as the effective fixed-separation estimation theorem and retain all stated scope disclaimers.

statements.proof_tex:
The three class relations are exactly \(\text{lem:jms-ace-class-relations}\).  In particular, the first inclusion is maximal in the direction needed here: every published ACE law is a member of the broad spectral class, whereas no reverse inclusion is used or claimed.

Assume \(\mathsf E_n^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) and \(\varepsilon_{1,n}>0\).  If \(\varepsilon_{2,n}>0\), the cited result \(\text{lem:jms-ace-quantile-upper}\) applies directly on the full class \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) and gives exactly
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}}
 Q_{P,1-\gamma}(|\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{ACE},r,n}-\theta_0(P)|)
 \le B_{\mathrm{ACE},n,\gamma}. \tag{1}
\]

Suppose instead that \(\varepsilon_{2,n}=0\).  For \(t\in(0,\varepsilon_{1,n})\), enlarge only the outcome-code radius from zero to \(t\).  Every law in the zero-radius class remains in the radius-\(t\) class.  Moreover,
\[
 \max\!\left\{\varepsilon_{1,n},t,
  (\gamma n)^{-1/2}(\psi_{\xi}+C_{\theta}\psi_{\eta})\right\}
 =
 \max\!\left\{\varepsilon_{1,n},0,
  (\gamma n)^{-1/2}(\psi_{\xi}+C_{\theta}\psi_{\eta})\right\}.
\]
Thus \(b_{2,n}\), and hence the eligibility predicate, is unchanged.  Apply the positive-radius cited theorem with radius \(t\), then restrict its supremum to the zero-radius class.  The resulting right-hand side differs from the claimed boundary value only by
\[
 C_{\gamma}r!16^r\delta^{-1}\varepsilon_{1,n}^rt.
\]
The published statistic is the same order-\(r\) ACE statistic for every radius.  Letting \(t\downarrow0\) proves (1) at the boundary.

Now also assume \(n\ge2\), \(\varepsilon_{1,n}\le\varepsilon_0\), and \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\neq\varnothing\).  By \(\text{lem:jms-ace-class-relations}\), this class is contained in \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\), so the latter is nonempty.  Restricting the generalized-quantile inequality in the proposed form of \(\text{thm:adaptive-rootn-minimax}\) to the subset gives
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}}
 Q_{P,1-\gamma}(|\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}-\theta_0(P)|)
 \le\sqrt{C/(\gamma n)}. \tag{2}
\]

Finally put
\[
 S_n=\varepsilon_{1,n}^r\varepsilon_{2,n}
     +C_{\theta}\varepsilon_{1,n}^{r+1}.
\]
All multiplicative quantities in \(B_{\mathrm{ACE},n,\gamma}\) other than \(S_n\) and \(n^{-1/2}\) are fixed positive class constants.  Along any eligible sequence for which \(S_n\gg n^{-1/2}\), (1) is therefore of order \(S_n\), while (2) is of order \(n^{-1/2}\).  Their ratio tends to zero.  This proves a strict comparison of the two displayed upper guarantees on the full published ACE class and, because no risk lower bound for the ACE statistic was used, proves the final caveat.
statements.justification: Probability-space norm monotonicity proves the comparison-class inclusion under exactly \(s\ge r\), after which the published theorem applies, including the zero outcome-radius boundary extension.
statements.gap: The broad spectral class does not impose the outcome-code or higher-norm conditions needed for the published ACE class.
statements.consumer: Apply the cited generalized-quantile upper bound directly on the full published ACE class and compare it there with the transported spectral upper guarantee. The comparison remains upper-versus-upper and gives no lower bound for the ACE estimator; the auxiliary \(L^s\) subclass only records the stronger-code comparison and equality at \(s=r\).

statements.statement:
The following are separate facts on separately defined, incomparable classes. Fix the same deterministic code pair \((\widehat g_n,\widehat q_n)\), its clipped pair \((\bar g_n,\bar q_n)\), and the same nested radii \((\varepsilon_{1,n},\varepsilon_{2,n})\) as external inputs. Under the certified-real input convention, compute and fix the once-for-all translated-dyadic bank and positive dyadic certificate supplied by \(\text{lem:finite-contour-bank}\). Along every sequence of indices \(n\to\infty\) for which \(n\ge2\), \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\neq\varnothing\), and \(\varepsilon_{1,n}\le\varepsilon_0\),
\[
 \mathfrak R_n^{\mathrm{NG}}\asymp n^{-1}.
\]
This includes fixed nonzero \(\varepsilon_{1,n}\). The witnessing total certified statistic \(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}\), as well as membership in \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\), imposes no restriction on and makes no use of \(\widehat q_n\), \(\bar q_n\), or \(\varepsilon_{2,n}\). Separately, every \(P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm G,n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) in the simultaneous bounded-observed-outcome Gaussian intersection of \(\text{def:gaussian-class}\) satisfies \(\theta_0(P)=0\). Whenever that intersection is nonempty,
\[
 \mathfrak R_n^{\mathrm G}
 =\mathfrak M_{n,1-\gamma}^{\mathrm G}
 =0.
\]
Thus \(\text{prop:bounded-outcome-gaussian-degeneracy}\) is solely a diagnostic of the simultaneous exact-PLM, bounded-\(Y\), and nondegenerate conditional-Gaussian assumptions stated around Jin--Mackey--Syrgkanis Theorem 3.2; its positive lower-bound claim is not used. These conclusions neither form a Gaussian-versus-non-Gaussian minimax dichotomy nor determine a local-to-Gaussian frontier, and no equality or inclusion between the two classes is asserted.
statements.proof_tex:
Apply \(\text{thm:adaptive-rootn-minimax}\). Its once-for-all bank is computed from certified-real primitive-constant names by \(\text{lem:finite-contour-bank}\), and on every index covered by the hypotheses,
\[
 \frac cn\le\mathfrak R_n^{\mathrm{NG}}\le\frac Cn.
\]
Hence \(\mathfrak R_n^{\mathrm{NG}}\asymp n^{-1}\) along every stated sequence, including a fixed nonzero treatment-code radius not exceeding \(\varepsilon_0\). Inspection of \(\text{def:non-gaussian-class}\) and \(\text{def:adaptive-contour-estimator}\) shows that both the class and the total certified statistic use \(\bar g_n\), while neither imposes a restriction involving nor uses \(\widehat q_n\), \(\bar q_n\), or \(\varepsilon_{2,n}\).

Separately, \(\text{prop:bounded-outcome-gaussian-degeneracy}\) proves that every member of \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm G,n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) has \(\theta_0(P)=0\). When that class is nonempty, the identically zero statistic has zero squared-error and generalized-quantile losses. Nonnegativity and \(\text{def:minimax-risks}\) therefore give
\[
 \mathfrak R_n^{\mathrm G}
 =\mathfrak M_{n,1-\gamma}^{\mathrm G}=0.
\]
That proposition uses only the simultaneous exact partially linear conditional mean, bounded observed outcome, and nondegenerate conditional-Gaussian restrictions; it does not use the source's positive lower-bound claim. Since the two conclusions concern separately defined classes and no inclusion or equality between them has been proved, they imply neither a Gaussian-versus-non-Gaussian minimax dichotomy nor a local-to-Gaussian frontier. This proves every scope qualification.
statements.justification: The theorem records the fixed-separated non-Gaussian rate and the Gaussian zero-target diagnostic as separate facts on separately defined classes.
statements.gap: The incomparable classes do not determine a local-to-Gaussian frontier.
statements.consumer: Do not describe the paired display as a Gaussian-versus-non-Gaussian minimax dichotomy.

statements.statement:
For every \(n\) such that \(\varepsilon_{1,n}\le 1/\pi\), let \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\stackrel{\mathrm{iid}}{\sim}P\). Suppose that \(\eta\sim\tfrac12N(-1,1)+\tfrac12N(1,1)\), \(\eta\perp X\), \(E_P[\xi\mid X,T]=0\) almost surely, \(|\theta_0(P)|\le C_{\theta}\), \(\|g_0\|_{\infty}\le C_g\), \(\|q_0\|_{\infty}\le C_q\), \(\|\xi\|_{\psi_2\mid X}\le\psi_{\xi}\) almost surely, and \(\|\bar g_n-g_0\|_{L^1(P_X)}\le\varepsilon_{1,n}\). Then \(\kappa_4(\eta)=-2\), \(M(i\pi/2)=0\), and
\[
E_P\!\left[Z_n\sin\!\left(\frac{\pi Z_n}{2}\right)\right]
=e^{-\pi^2/8}E_P\!\left[\cos\!\left(\frac{\pi D_n}{2}\right)\right]
\ge \frac12e^{-\pi^2/8}.
\]
There is a finite constant \(C\), depending only on \(C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\xi}\), such that, uniformly over all laws \(P\) satisfying the preceding conditions,
\[
E_P\!\left[(\widehat\theta_{\sin,n}-\theta_0(P))^2\right]\le \frac{C}{n}.
\]
No condition on the supplied outcome code or on \(\varepsilon_{2,n}\) is required.
statements.proof_tex:
Put \(a=\pi/2\). Represent the stipulated mixture as \(\eta=R+E\), where \(R\) is symmetric Rademacher, \(E\sim N(0,1)\), and \(R\perp E\). Then
\[
M(z)=E_P[e^{z\eta}]=e^{z^2/2}\cosh z,
\qquad
M(ia)=e^{-a^2/2}\cos a=0.
\]
Moreover, \(E_P[\eta]=0\), \(E_P[\eta^2]=2\), and independence gives
\[
E_P[\eta^4]
=E_P[R^4]+6E_P[R^2]E_P[E^2]+E_P[E^4]
=1+6+3=10.
\]
The centered fourth-cumulant identity therefore yields
\[
\kappa_4(\eta)=E_P[\eta^4]-3E_P[\eta^2]^2=10-3\cdot2^2=-2.
\]

The characteristic function of \(\eta\) is
\[
\phi(t)=E_P[e^{it\eta}]=e^{-t^2/2}\cos t.
\]
For any deterministic \(d\in\mathbb R\), symmetry of \(\eta\) gives
\[
E_P[\cos\{t(\eta+d)\}]=\phi(t)\cos(td).
\]
Differentiation under the expectation is valid because the Gaussian mixture has a finite first moment. Hence
\[
E_P[(\eta+d)\sin\{t(\eta+d)\}]
=-\frac{d}{dt}\{\phi(t)\cos(td)\}.
\]
Since \(\phi(a)=0\) and \(\phi'(a)=-e^{-a^2/2}\), evaluation at \(a=\pi/2\) gives
\[
E_P[(\eta+d)\sin\{a(\eta+d)\}]
=e^{-a^2/2}\cos(ad).
\]
The variable \(D_n\) is measurable with respect to \(X\), so \(\eta\perp X\) implies \(\eta\perp D_n\). Conditioning on \(D_n\) and using \(Z_n=\eta+D_n\),
\[
E_P[Z_n\sin(aZ_n)]
=e^{-a^2/2}E_P[\cos(aD_n)]
=e^{-\pi^2/8}E_P[\cos(\pi D_n/2)].
\]
The direct \(L^1(P_X)\) premise is exactly
\[
E_P|D_n|=\|\bar g_n-g_0\|_{L^1(P_X)}\le\varepsilon_{1,n}.
\]
Using \(1-\cos u\le |u|\) and \(\varepsilon_{1,n}\le1/\pi\),
\[
E_P[\cos(aD_n)]
\ge1-aE_P|D_n|
\ge1-\frac{\pi}{2}\frac1\pi
=\frac12.
\]
Thus
\[
c_0:=\frac12e^{-\pi^2/8}>0
\]
is a uniform population relevance and division bound. The cutoff in \(\widehat\theta_{\sin,n}\) prevents division below \(c_0/2\).

For the risk calculation define
\[
W_i:=Z_{n,i}\sin(aZ_{n,i}),
\qquad
V_i:=\{Y_i-\theta_0(P)Z_{n,i}\}\sin(aZ_{n,i}),
\]
and let \(\bar W_n=\mathbb P_nW\) and \(\bar V_n=\mathbb P_nV\). The residual identity is
\[
Y-\theta_0(P)Z_n=b_n(X)+\xi,
\qquad
b_n(X)=q_0(X)-\theta_0(P)D_n.
\]
For every \(d\in\mathbb R\),
\[
E_P[\sin\{a(\eta+d)\}]
=\operatorname{Im}\{e^{iad}\phi(a)\}=0.
\]
Consequently, conditioning on \(X\) gives
\[
E_P[b_n(X)\sin(aZ_n)]=0.
\]
Because \(Z_n=T-\bar g_n(X)\) is measurable with respect to \((X,T)\), the conditional-mean restriction gives
\[
E_P[\xi\sin(aZ_n)]
=E_P\!\left[E_P[\xi\mid X,T]\sin(aZ_n)\right]=0.
\]
Therefore \(E_P[V_i]=0\).

The clipping definition and the range restriction imply \(|D_n|\le2C_g\) almost surely. Set
\[
b_{\max}:=C_q+2C_{\theta}C_g.
\]
Then \(|b_n(X)|\le b_{\max}\). The conditional sub-Gaussian condition entails \(E_P[\xi^2]\le K_{\xi}\psi_{\xi}^2\) for a finite universal constant \(K_{\xi}\) determined only by the convention for the conditional \(\psi_2\)-norm. Since \(|\sin u|\le1\),
\[
E_P[V_i^2]
\le2b_{\max}^2+2K_{\xi}\psi_{\xi}^2
=:K_V.
\]
Also, \(E_P[\eta^2]=2\), \(|D_n|\le2C_g\), and \(|\sin u|\le1\) imply
\[
E_P[W_i^2]
\le E_P[Z_n^2]
\le2E_P[\eta^2]+2E_P[D_n^2]
\le4+8C_g^2
=:K_W.
\]
These bounds verify the integrability needed for conditioning, differentiation, and the variance calculations.

Let \(\mathcal A_n=\{\bar W_n\ge c_0/2\}\), the event on which the sample ratio is used. Projection onto \([-C_{\theta},C_{\theta}]\) cannot increase distance from \(\theta_0(P)\). Thus, on \(\mathcal A_n\),
\[
|\widehat\theta_{\sin,n}-\theta_0(P)|^2
\le\frac{\bar V_n^2}{\bar W_n^2}
\le\frac{4\bar V_n^2}{c_0^2}.
\]
On \(\mathcal A_n^c\), clipping bounds the squared loss by \(4C_{\theta}^2\). If \(m_W=E_P[W_i]\), then \(m_W\ge c_0\). Independent and identically distributed sampling and Chebyshev's inequality therefore give
\[
P(\mathcal A_n^c)
\le P\!\left(|\bar W_n-m_W|\ge\frac{c_0}{2}\right)
\le\frac{4\operatorname{Var}_P(W_i)}{nc_0^2}
\le\frac{4K_W}{nc_0^2}.
\]
The same sampling condition and \(E_P[V_i]=0\) yield
\[
E_P[\bar V_n^2]
=\frac{\operatorname{Var}_P(V_i)}{n}
\le\frac{K_V}{n}.
\]
Combining the two events,
\[
\begin{aligned}
E_P[(\widehat\theta_{\sin,n}-\theta_0(P))^2]
&\le\frac{4K_V}{nc_0^2}
+4C_{\theta}^2\frac{4K_W}{nc_0^2}\\
&=\frac{4K_V+16C_{\theta}^2K_W}{c_0^2}\,\frac1n.
\end{aligned}
\]
The constant depends only on \(C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\xi}\), and not on \(P\), \(n\), the supplied outcome code, or \(\varepsilon_{2,n}\). This proves the proposition, including its support, relevance, positivity, integrability, and fallback boundary conditions.
statements.justification: This bounded-score reduction exposes exact annihilation and root-\(n\) risk without contour selection.
statements.gap: Finite-order polynomial orthogonality does not use the characteristic-function zero to annihilate every covariate shift exactly.
statements.consumer: The mixture provides a reproducible benchmark and a simple implementation for symmetric non-Gaussian residuals.

statements.statement: For triangular treatment-noise laws with \(|\kappa_k(\eta_n)|\ge\delta_n\downarrow0\) under the same supplied code sequences, does there exist a data-driven selector among ordinary DML, finite-order ACE, and global-contour procedures that attains the sharp minimax mean-squared-error rate as a function of \((n,\varepsilon_{1,n},\varepsilon_{2,n},\delta_n)\), yields uniformly valid inference across these regimes, and admits a matching local minimax lower bound?
statements.justification: The open question isolates the scientifically relevant weak-spectral boundary after the fixed-separation theorem is closed.
statements.gap: Only local ACE and explicit-path upper benchmarks are known; adaptation, coverage, and matching lower bounds remain open.
statements.consumer: Treat this as the residual research agenda, not as an established phase diagram.

statements.statement:
Specialize to \(k=4\).  For \(0<a\le1\), let
\[
 \eta_a=\sqrt{1-a^2}\,G_{\circ}+aS,
 \qquad
 t_a=\frac{\pi}{2a},
 \qquad
 A_a=a\exp\!\left\{-\frac{(1-a^2)\pi^2}{8a^2}\right\},
\]
where \(G_{\circ}\sim N(0,1)\), \(S\) is symmetric Rademacher, and \(G_{\circ}\perp S\).  Consider any law satisfying \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\stackrel{\mathrm{iid}}{\sim}P\), \(\eta=\eta_a\perp X\), \(E_P[\xi\mid X,T]=0\) almost surely, \(\lvert\theta_0(P)\rvert\le C_{\theta}\), \(\lVert g_0\rVert_{\infty}\le C_g\), \(\lVert q_0\rVert_{\infty}\le C_q\), \(\lVert\xi\rVert_{\psi_2\mid X}\le\psi_{\xi}\) almost surely, and the direct condition \(\lVert\bar g_n-g_0\rVert_{L^1(P_X)}\le\varepsilon_{1,n}\).  Then
\[
 M_a(z)=\exp\!\left(\frac{1-a^2}{2}z^2\right)\cosh(az),
 \qquad
 \kappa_4(\eta_a)=-2a^4,
\]
\(t_a\) is the first positive characteristic zero, and \(E[\sin\{t_a(\eta_a+d)\}]=0\) for every real \(d\).  If \(t_a\varepsilon_{1,n}\le1/2\), then
\[
 E_P[Z_n\sin(t_aZ_n)]
 =A_aE_P[\cos(t_aD_n)]
 \ge A_a/2.
\]
Define
\[
 \widehat\theta_{a,n}
 =
 \begin{cases}
 \displaystyle
 \Pi_{[-C_{\theta},C_{\theta}]}
 \frac{\mathbb P_n[Y\sin(t_aZ_n)]}
      {\mathbb P_n[Z_n\sin(t_aZ_n)]},
 &\displaystyle \mathbb P_n[Z_n\sin(t_aZ_n)]\ge A_a/4,\\[3mm]
 0,&\text{otherwise}.
 \end{cases}
\]
There is \(C<\infty\), depending only on \(C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\xi}\), such that uniformly over these laws,
\[
 E_P[(\widehat\theta_{a,n}-\theta_0(P))^2]
 \le C\min\!\left\{1,\frac1n a^{-2}
 \exp\!\left(\frac{(1-a^2)\pi^2}{4a^2}\right)\right\}.
\]
Equivalently, for \(\Delta_a=2a^4\), the condition is \(\varepsilon_{1,n}\le\Delta_a^{1/4}/(2^{1/4}\pi)\), and the risk is at most
\[
 C\min\!\left\{1,\frac1n\Delta_a^{-1/2}
 \exp\!\left(\frac{\pi^2\sqrt2}{4}\Delta_a^{-1/2}\right)\right\}.
\]
statements.proof_tex:
Independence of \(G_{\circ}\) and \(S\) gives
\[
 M_a(z)
 =E[e^{z\sqrt{1-a^2}G_{\circ}}]E[e^{zaS}]
 =\exp\!\left(\frac{1-a^2}{2}z^2\right)\cosh(az).
\]
Since the fourth derivative at zero of \(\log\cosh(az)\) is \(-2a^4\), the cumulant definition gives \(\kappa_4(\eta_a)=-2a^4\).  Its characteristic function is
\[
 \varphi_a(t)=M_a(it)
 =\exp\!\left(-\frac{1-a^2}{2}t^2\right)\cos(at).
\]
The exponential factor is positive, so the first positive zero is \(t_a=\pi/(2a)\), and for every real \(d\),
\[
 E[\sin\{t_a(\eta_a+d)\}]
 =\operatorname{Im}\{e^{it_ad}\varphi_a(t_a)\}=0.
\]
Moreover,
\[
 \varphi_a'(t_a)
 =-a\exp\!\left\{-\frac{(1-a^2)\pi^2}{8a^2}\right\}=-A_a.
\]
Differentiation under the expectation is justified because \(\eta_a\) has moments of every order.  Differentiating \(e^{itd}\varphi_a(t)\) and taking real parts at \(t_a\) yields
\[
 E[(\eta_a+d)\sin\{t_a(\eta_a+d)\}]=A_a\cos(t_ad).
\]
Since \(D_n\) is measurable in \(X\) and \(\eta_a\perp X\), conditioning on \(D_n\) gives
\[
 m_a:=E_P[Z_n\sin(t_aZ_n)]=A_aE_P[\cos(t_aD_n)].
\]
The direct \(L^1(P_X)\) premise is exactly \(E_P|D_n|\le\varepsilon_{1,n}\).  Hence \(1-\cos u\le|u|\) and \(t_a\varepsilon_{1,n}\le1/2\) imply
\[
 E_P[\cos(t_aD_n)]
 \ge1-t_aE_P|D_n|
 \ge\frac12,
\]
so \(m_a\ge A_a/2>0\).  This is the required overlap condition.

Put
\[
 W=Z_n\sin(t_aZ_n),\qquad
 V=Y\sin(t_aZ_n),\qquad
 R=(Y-\theta_0Z_n)\sin(t_aZ_n).
\]
The residual identity is \(Y-\theta_0Z_n=b_n(X)+\xi\).  Conditional shift annihilation gives
\[
 E_P[b_n(X)\sin(t_aZ_n)]=0,
\]
and outcome mean independence gives
\[
 E_P[\xi\sin(t_aZ_n)]
 =E_P[\sin(t_aZ_n)E_P(\xi\mid X,T)]=0.
\]
Therefore \(E_P[R]=0\) and \(E_P[V]=\theta_0m_a\), establishing the population identifying moment separately from the sample ratio.

Clipping and the range condition give \(|D_n|\le2C_g\).  Since \(E[\eta_a^2]=1\) and \(\eta_a\perp D_n\),
\[
 E_P[W^2]\le E_P[Z_n^2]
 =1+E_P[D_n^2]\le1+4C_g^2=:K_W.
\]
Also \(|b_n(X)|\le C_q+2C_{\theta}C_g\).  The conditional sub-Gaussian premise implies \(E_P[\xi^2]\le c_{\psi}\psi_{\xi}^2\) for a universal convention-dependent \(c_{\psi}<\infty\).  Thus
\[
 E_P[R^2]
 \le2(C_q+2C_{\theta}C_g)^2+2c_{\psi}\psi_{\xi}^2=:K_R.
\]
Both constants are uniform in \(a,n,P\).

Write \(\overline W=\mathbb P_nW\), \(\overline V=\mathbb P_nV\), and \(\mathcal E=\{\overline W\ge A_a/4\}\).  Projection onto \([-C_{\theta},C_{\theta}]\) is a contraction and \(\theta_0\) belongs to that interval.  On \(\mathcal E\),
\[
 |\widehat\theta_{a,n}-\theta_0|
 \le\frac{|\mathbb P_nR|}{\overline W}
 \le\frac4{A_a}|\mathbb P_nR|.
\]
Independence and \(E_P[R]=0\) yield
\[
 E_P[(\mathbb P_nR)^2]\le K_R/n.
\]
On \(\mathcal E^c\), the squared error is at most \(C_{\theta}^2\), while Chebyshev's inequality and \(m_a\ge A_a/2\) give
\[
 P(\mathcal E^c)
 \le P(|\overline W-m_a|\ge A_a/4)
 \le\frac{16K_W}{nA_a^2}.
\]
Consequently
\[
 E_P[(\widehat\theta_{a,n}-\theta_0)^2]
 \le\frac{16(K_R+C_{\theta}^2K_W)}{nA_a^2}.
\]
The independent deterministic bound \(|\widehat\theta_{a,n}-\theta_0|^2\le4C_{\theta}^2\), together with
\[
 A_a^{-2}=a^{-2}\exp\!\left\{\frac{(1-a^2)\pi^2}{4a^2}\right\},
\]
proves the first risk display.  Finally \(\Delta_a=2a^4\) gives
\[
 a=2^{-1/4}\Delta_a^{1/4},
 \qquad
 t_a\varepsilon_{1,n}\le\frac12
 \Longleftrightarrow
 \varepsilon_{1,n}\le\frac{\Delta_a^{1/4}}{2^{1/4}\pi},
\]
and
\[
 a^{-2}\exp\!\left\{\frac{(1-a^2)\pi^2}{4a^2}\right\}
 =\sqrt2e^{-\pi^2/4}\Delta_a^{-1/2}
 \exp\!\left\{\frac{\pi^2\sqrt2}{4}\Delta_a^{-1/2}\right\}.
\]
Absorbing the fixed prefactor into \(C\) completes the proof.  No supplied outcome code is used.

statements.statement:
For \(n\ge2\), there is \(K<\infty\), depending only on \(C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\eta},\psi_{\xi}\), and \(R_1\), such that, for every \(P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\) and every \(a\in\{0,1\}\) with \(|I_a|\ge1\),
\[
 E_P\!\left[\sup_{|z|\le R_1}|\widehat F_{a,n}(z)-F_n(z)|^2\right]
 +E_P\!\left[\sup_{|z|\le R_1}|\widehat G_{a,n}(z)-G_n(z)|^2\right]
 \le \frac{K}{|I_a|}.
\]
statements.proof_tex:
Let \(m=|I_a|\) and put \(B=2C_g\).  Under the exact Luxemburg convention, for every \(p>0\),
\[
 E_P|W|^p\le 2\sigma^p\Gamma(p/2+1) \tag{1}
\]
when \(W=\eta,\sigma=\psi_\eta\), and also when \(W=\xi,\sigma=\psi_\xi\) after integrating the conditional bound.  Define \(A_0=C_0=1\) and, for \(j\ge1\),
\[
 A_j=2^{j-1/2}\{2\psi_\eta^{2j}j!+B^{2j}\}^{1/2},\qquad
 C_j=2^{j-1/4}\{2\psi_\eta^{4j}(2j)!+B^{4j}\}^{1/4}.
\]
Since \(Z_n=\eta+D_n\) and \(|D_n|\le B\), (1) and \(|x+y|^p\le2^{p-1}(|x|^p+|y|^p)\) give \(\|Z_n^j\|_2\le A_j\) and \(\|Z_n^j\|_4\le C_j\).  Moreover, \(\|\eta\|_4\le\sqrt2\psi_\eta\) and \(\|\xi\|_4\le\sqrt2\psi_\xi\).  Hence, with \(Y=q_0(X)+\theta_0\eta+\xi\), Hölder's inequality gives, without requiring independence between \(\xi\) and \(\eta\),
\[
 \|YZ_n^j\|_2\le C_qA_j+\sqrt2(C_\theta\psi_\eta+\psi_\xi)C_j=:H_j. \tag{2}
\]
Set
\[
 S_F=\sum_{j\ge0}\frac{R_1^jA_j}{j!},\qquad S_G=\sum_{j\ge0}\frac{R_1^jH_j}{j!}.
\]
Both series are finite.  Indeed,
\[
 A_j\le2^j\psi_\eta^j\sqrt{j!}+2^{j-1/2}B^j,\quad
 C_j\le2^j\psi_\eta^j((2j)!)^{1/4}+2^{j-1/4}B^j,
\]
and the ratios of the two factorial-denominator terms tend to zero, while the remaining terms are dominated by exponential series.

For \(h_j=Z_n^j\) or \(h_j=YZ_n^j\), independence of the observations and the variance bound by the second moment give
\[
 \|(\mathbb P_{I_a}-P)h_j\|_2\le m^{-1/2}\|h_j\|_2. \tag{3}
\]
Apply the triangle inequality and Minkowski's inequality in the correct direction to finite power-series truncations, use (2)--(3), and pass to the limit by the displayed summable majorants.  This yields
\[
 \left\|\sup_{|z|\le R_1}|\widehat F_{a,n}(z)-F_n(z)|\right\|_2\le\frac{S_F}{\sqrt m},\qquad
 \left\|\sup_{|z|\le R_1}|\widehat G_{a,n}(z)-G_n(z)|\right\|_2\le\frac{S_G}{\sqrt m}.
\]
Squaring and adding proves the claim with the explicit finite constant \(K=S_F^2+S_G^2\), depending only on the listed primitive constants and \(R_1\).

statements.statement:
For every \(P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\), the class's \(L^1(P_X)\) treatment-code restriction and clipping imply \(|D_n|\le2C_g\) almost surely and \(E_P|D_n|\le\varepsilon_{1,n}\). Hence
\[
 \sup_{|z|\le R_1}|H_n(z)-1|
 \le R_1e^{2C_gR_1}\varepsilon_{1,n}.
\]
If \(\varepsilon_{1,n}\le\varepsilon_0\), then \(|H_n(z)|\ge3/4\) throughout \(\{|z|\le R_1\}\), and \(F_n=M H_n\) and \(M\) have the same zeros there with multiplicity.
statements.proof_tex:
Both \(g_0(X)\) and \(\bar g_n(X)\) lie in \([-C_g,C_g]\), so \(|D_n|\le2C_g\) almost surely.  The class restriction is exactly \(E_P|D_n|\le\varepsilon_{1,n}\).  For \(|z|\le R_1\), the identity
\(e^{zD_n}-1=zD_n\int_0^1e^{tzD_n}\,dt\) gives
\[
 |H_n(z)-1|
 \le |z|E_P[|D_n|e^{|z||D_n|}]
 \le R_1e^{2C_gR_1}\varepsilon_{1,n}.
\]
If \(\varepsilon_{1,n}\le\varepsilon_0=(4R_1e^{2C_gR_1})^{-1}\), the right side is at most \(1/4\); hence \(|H_n(z)|\ge3/4\) on the whole disk.  The factorization lemma gives \(F_n=MH_n\).  Since the second factor is holomorphic and nowhere zero there, multiplication by it neither creates nor removes zeros and preserves every zero multiplicity.

statements.statement:
The following two conclusions are valid, but they do not determine the full-class minimax phase diagram.

First, for each \(n\), let \(\mathcal C_n(\delta_n)\) be the class obtained from \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) in \(\text{def:jms-ace-class}\) by replacing the fixed restriction \(\lvert\kappa_{r+1}(\eta)\rvert\ge\delta\) by \(\lvert\kappa_{r+1}(\eta)\rvert\ge\delta_n\), without changing any other restriction.  Define
\[
 \widetilde b_{2,n}
 =200\min\{1,C_{\theta}\}\delta_n
 \max\!\left\{
   \varepsilon_{1,n},\varepsilon_{2,n},
   (\gamma n)^{-1/2}(\psi_{\xi}+C_{\theta}\psi_{\eta})
 \right\}^{-1}.
\]
Suppose \(\varepsilon_{1,n},\varepsilon_{2,n}>0\), all logarithms and denominators in the following display are defined, and the exact local eligibility condition
\[
 r\le
 \min\!\left\{
   \frac{b_{1,n}}{a_{1,n}}
   -\frac{1}{a_{1,n}}\log\!\left(\frac{b_{1,n}}{a_{1,n}}\right),
   \frac{\widetilde b_{2,n}}{a_2\log(a_2\widetilde b_{2,n})}
 \right\}
\]
holds.  Then the order-\(r\) ACE estimator obeys the local oracle benchmark
\[
\begin{aligned}
 &\sup_{P\in\mathcal C_n(\delta_n)}
 Q_{P,1-\gamma}
 \!\left(\left|\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{ACE},r,n}-\theta_0(P)\right|\right)\\
 &\quad\le
 C_{\gamma}r!16^r\delta_n^{-1}
 \Bigl[
   \varepsilon_{1,n}^r\varepsilon_{2,n}
   +C_{\theta}\varepsilon_{1,n}^{r+1}\\
 &\hspace{42mm}
   +64(C_g+\psi_{\eta})^r
    \{r^2(C_g+\psi_{\eta})+\psi_{\xi}+C_{\theta}\psi_{\eta}\}
    (\gamma n)^{-1/2}
 \Bigr].
\end{aligned}
\]
Denote the right-hand side by \(U_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{loc}}\).  If \(U_{\mathrm{DML},n}\) denotes a separately valid ordinary-DML upper bound under its own hypotheses, then \(\min\{U_{\mathrm{DML},n},U_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{loc}}\}\) is only an oracle upper envelope; this comparison neither asserts a minimax rate nor constructs a data-driven selector.

Second, specialize to \(k=4\), hence \(r=3\).  For \(0<a\le1\), let
\[
 \eta_a=\sqrt{1-a^2}\,G_{\circ}+aS,
\]
where \(G_{\circ}\sim N(0,1)\), \(S\) is symmetric Rademacher, and \(G_{\circ}\perp S\).  Its moment generating function, fourth cumulant, and first positive characteristic zero are
\[
 M_a(z)=\exp\!\left(\frac{1-a^2}{2}z^2\right)\cosh(az),
 \qquad
 \kappa_4(\eta_a)=-2a^4,
 \qquad
 t_a=\frac{\pi}{2a}.
\]
For every real \(d\),
\[
 E\!\left[\sin\{t_a(\eta_a+d)\}\right]=0.
\]
Consider any law satisfying \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\stackrel{\mathrm{iid}}{\sim}P\), \(\eta=\eta_a\perp X\), \(E_P[\xi\mid X,T]=0\) almost surely, \(\lvert\theta_0(P)\rvert\le C_{\theta}\), \(\lVert g_0\rVert_{\infty}\le C_g\), \(\lVert q_0\rVert_{\infty}\le C_q\), \(\lVert\xi\rVert_{\psi_2\mid X}\le\psi_{\xi}\) almost surely, and \(\lVert\bar g_n-g_0\rVert_{L^1(P_X)}\le\varepsilon_{1,n}\).  Put
\[
 A_a=a\exp\!\left\{-\frac{(1-a^2)\pi^2}{8a^2}\right\}.
\]
If \(t_a\varepsilon_{1,n}\le1/2\), then
\[
 E_P\!\left[Z_n\sin(t_aZ_n)\right]
 =A_aE_P[\cos(t_aD_n)]
 \ge\frac{A_a}{2}.
\]
Writing \(\mathbb P_n\) for the empirical average, define the computable clipped ratio
\[
 \widehat\theta_{a,n}
 =
 \begin{cases}
 \displaystyle
 \Pi_{[-C_{\theta},C_{\theta}]}
 \frac{\mathbb P_n[Y\sin(t_aZ_n)]}
      {\mathbb P_n[Z_n\sin(t_aZ_n)]},
 &\displaystyle
 \mathbb P_n[Z_n\sin(t_aZ_n)]\ge A_a/4,\\[3mm]
 0,&\text{otherwise}.
 \end{cases}
\]
There is a finite constant \(C\), depending only on \(C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\xi}\), such that
\[
 \sup_P E_P\!\left[(\widehat\theta_{a,n}-\theta_0(P))^2\right]
 \le
 C\min\!\left\{
  1,\frac{1}{n}a^{-2}
  \exp\!\left(\frac{(1-a^2)\pi^2}{4a^2}\right)
 \right\},
\]
where the supremum is over the just-displayed path laws.  Equivalently, with \(\Delta_a=2a^4=\lvert\kappa_4(\eta_a)\rvert\), the condition \(t_a\varepsilon_{1,n}\le1/2\) is
\[
 \varepsilon_{1,n}\le\frac{\Delta_a^{1/4}}{2^{1/4}\pi},
\]
and the preceding risk is at most
\[
 C\min\!\left\{
  1,\frac{1}{n}\Delta_a^{-1/2}
  \exp\!\left(\frac{\pi^2\sqrt2}{4}\Delta_a^{-1/2}\right)
 \right\}.
\]
This last display is a construction-specific upper bound with \(\varepsilon_{1,n}=O(\Delta_a^{1/4})\); it is not asserted to be sharp for the class specified only by a fourth-cumulant lower bound.
statements.justification: This is the strongest closed local-to-Gaussian result supported by the current proof spine: an exact published ACE specialization and an explicit pathwise spectral upper bound.
statements.gap: It supplies upper benchmarks but no full cumulant-only converse, quantitative contour-modulus theorem, adaptive switching theorem, or coverage result.
statements.consumer: A downstream analysis can use the displayed eligibility test and risk formula to compare finite-order and pathwise spectral procedures without mistaking either for the unresolved minimax frontier.
statements.proof_tex:
For the first conclusion, apply the universally quantified published theorem recorded in \(\text{lem:jms-ace-theorem-five-four}\) with its separation constant specialized to \(\delta_n\).  This substitution changes \(b_{2,n}\) exactly to \(\widetilde b_{2,n}\), leaves every other hypothesis unchanged, and changes the leading inverse-separation factor exactly to \(\delta_n^{-1}\).  The stated eligibility condition and the displayed local ACE bound follow verbatim.  Taking a minimum with a separately valid DML bound is only a pointwise oracle comparison; no data-dependent selector or converse follows from two upper inequalities.

For the second conclusion, specialize \(r=3\), hence \(k=4\), and invoke \(\text{lem:gaussian-rademacher-l1-benchmark}\), whose assumptions are exactly the path assumptions displayed here.  That lemma proves the transform formula, cumulant, zero, all-shift sine annihilation, denominator overlap, construction of the clipped ratio, and both equivalent risk displays.  Therefore both asserted benchmarks hold.  Neither argument supplies a lower bound for the full cumulant-only triangular class, so the final scope qualification follows.

statements.justification: The simultaneous Gaussian conditions force the target to vanish and therefore invalidate the former positive lower-bound arm.
statements.gap: The published Gaussian lower bound cannot be transferred to an intersection whose target is identically zero.
statements.consumer: The corrected common-experiment theorem uses this proposition to compute both Gaussian losses exactly.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm G,n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\). By the residual definitions,
\[
 Y=q_0(X)+\theta_0\eta+\xi.
\]
The restriction \(E_P[\xi\mid X,T]=0\) and the identity \(\eta=T-g_0(X)\) imply
\[
 E_P[Y\mid X,T]=q_0(X)+\theta_0\eta. \tag{1}
\]
Since \(|Y|\le C_q\) almost surely, conditional Jensen gives
\[
 |q_0(X)+\theta_0\eta|
 =|E_P[Y\mid X,T]|le C_q
 \quad\text{almost surely}. \tag{2}
\]
The Gaussian-class assumptions give \(\eta\perp X\) and \(\eta\sim N(0,\sigma^2)\) with \(\sigma>0\). If \(\theta_0\ne0\), then for every finite real number \(u\), the nondegenerate Gaussian variable \(u+\theta_0\eta\) has unbounded support, and therefore
\[
 P(|u+\theta_0\eta|>C_q)>0. \tag{3}
\]
Taking \(u=q_0(x)\) and using independence, (3) holds for \(P_X\)-almost every conditional law given \(X=x\), contradicting (2). Hence \(\theta_0(P)=0\).

If the class is nonempty, the statistic identically equal to zero has squared error zero under every member. It also has absolute error zero almost surely, so its generalized quantile is zero. Both minimax losses are nonnegative by definition; consequently
\[
 \mathfrak R_n^{\mathrm G}
 =\mathfrak M_{n,1-\gamma}^{\mathrm G}=0.
\]
Thus the zero statistic is minimax for both displayed losses.

statements.statement:
For every \(n\),
\[
 \mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}
 \subseteq \mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}.
\]
For \(s\ge r\),
\[
 \mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}^{\mathrm{ACE}}
 \subseteq \mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}},
\]
and, under the common clipped-code convention in the displayed class definitions, equality holds when \(s=r\).
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(n\).  First let \(P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\).  Every structural, range, tail, independence, and cumulant condition in \(\text{def:non-gaussian-class}\) occurs verbatim in \(\text{def:jms-ace-class}\).  The only condition of the former definition that is not literally displayed with the same exponent in the latter is the direct treatment-code restriction.  Since \(P_X\) is a probability law and \(r\ge2\), H\"older's inequality gives
\[
 \|\bar g_n-g_0\|_{L^1(P_X)}
 \le \|\bar g_n-g_0\|_{L^r(P_X)}
 \le \varepsilon_{1,n}.
\]
The broad class imposes no supplied outcome-code restriction.  Hence \(P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\), proving
\[
 \mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}
 \subseteq\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}. \tag{1}
\]

Now suppose \(s\ge r\) and let \(P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}^{\mathrm{ACE}}\).  On the probability space \((\mathcal X,\mathcal A,P_X)\), norm monotonicity gives
\[
 \|f\|_{L^r(P_X)}\le \|f\|_{L^s(P_X)},
\]
with the essential-supremum interpretation when \(s=\infty\).  Apply this inequality to \(f=\bar g_n-g_0\) and to \(f=\bar q_n-q_0\).  The two \(L^s(P_X)\) restrictions in \(\text{def:ace-comparison-subclass}\) therefore imply the two \(L^r(P_X)\) restrictions in \(\text{def:jms-ace-class}\), while all other conditions are inherited from \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\).  Thus
\[
 \mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}^{\mathrm{ACE}}
 \subseteq\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}. \tag{2}
\]

Finally suppose \(s=r\).  Inclusion (2) remains valid.  Conversely, (1) places every member of \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) in \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\), and its two defining \(L^r(P_X)\) code bounds are exactly the two additional restrictions defining \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}^{\mathrm{ACE}}\) when \(s=r\).  Because the same clipped functions \(\bar g_n\) and \(\bar q_n\) occur in both definitions, this proves the reverse inclusion and hence equality.

sampling_model.design: For each \(n\), the externally supplied deterministic code pair is fixed before \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\stackrel{\mathrm{iid}}{\sim}P\) is drawn. The spectral algorithm receives canonical dyadic names of \(T_i\), \(Y_i\), and \(\bar g_n(X_i)\), internally computes the bank from canonical certified names of \(k,\delta,\psi_{\eta},R_0,R_1\), and derives every empirical transform, derivative, Lipschitz, winding, and final-integrand enclosure by finite outward rational refinement. It receives neither an externally selected bank nor the treatment-noise law.
sampling_model.treatment: Continuous treatment with \(\eta=T-g_0(X)\). The fixed-separated spectral class imposes independent cumulant-separated sub-Gaussian treatment noise. The separate Gaussian intersection reproduces simultaneous known-variance and bounded-observed-outcome assumptions used only for the source-assumption diagnostic.
sampling_model.overlap: No propensity-score overlap condition is used. Spectral relevance is expressed by a positive winding number and a contour boundary modulus bounded away from zero; the Gaussian degeneracy proof uses bounded outcome support and nondegenerate Gaussian support.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The deterministic radii \(\varepsilon_{1,n}\) and \(\varepsilon_{2,n}\) are nonincreasing. The broad spectral class and estimator require only sufficiently small direct \(L^1(P_X)\) treatment-code error and impose no supplied outcome-code restriction. The full published ACE class has stronger \(L^r(P_X)\) treatment- and outcome-code restrictions and is therefore contained in the broad spectral class. The auxiliary class \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}^{\mathrm{ACE}}\) adds both \(L^s(P_X)\) restrictions; it is a subclass for \(s\ge r\) and equals the published ACE class at \(s=r\).

estimand_functional: Under the standard certified-real input convention, the certified translated-dyadic bank and certified statistic define a computable observed-sample map from the supplied primitive-constant names such that, for every \(n\ge2\) with \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\neq\varnothing\) and \(\varepsilon_{1,n}\le\varepsilon_0\), \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}}E_P[(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}-\theta_0(P))^2]\le C/n\).
