tldr: For fixed nonzero cumulant separation, a once-for-all certified translated-dyadic contour bank and a total split-sample statistic identify and estimate the partially linear causal coefficient with uniform matched \(\Theta(n^{-1})\) mean-squared error using only a sufficiently accurate direct \(L^1(P_X)\) treatment code, no outcome learner, and no knowledge of the treatment-noise law. An ACE-preserving outcome-tilt converse and the spectral upper bound give the same matched minimax order on the full published ACE class, while the cited ACE-versus-spectral generalized-quantile comparison remains strictly upper-versus-upper. The bounded-outcome Gaussian calculation is only a source-assumption diagnostic: the simultaneous stated restrictions force \(\theta_0=0\).

project_justification.gap: Finite-order orthogonal and ACE methods provide nuisance-dependent upper guarantees, while classical location-family work recognizes transform zeros; neither supplies the present learned-residual contour estimator with an explicit certified translated-dyadic bank and matched fixed-separation minimax MSE. The published ACE class does embed in the broad direct-\(L^1(P_X)\) spectral class, which licenses a full-class upper-guarantee comparison but not an ACE lower bound. The simultaneous bounded-outcome Gaussian assumptions around Jin--Mackey--Syrgkanis Theorem 3.2 instead force the target to vanish and therefore serve only as a source-assumption diagnostic.
project_justification.niche: Independent cumulant-separated sub-Gaussian treatment noise creates an exact null space for every location shift induced by treatment-code error. A sufficiently small fixed direct \(L^1(P_X)\) residual contamination preserves observable zero geometry, while certified-real primitive constants suffice to compute a uniformly conditioned contour bank without the unknown noise law. Because an \(L^r(P_X)\) treatment-code guarantee implies this \(L^1(P_X)\) condition, the construction applies throughout the full published ACE comparison class.
project_justification.fill: The paper proves exact annihilator and observable contour identities, the numerical zero radius, a terminating certified translated-dyadic bank construction with a positive dyadic modulus, empirical-transform control, a total certified statistic, and matching \(c/n\) and \(C/n\) MSE bounds on the broad spectral class. By preserving both published \(L^r(P_X)\) code restrictions in the outcome-tilt submodel, it also proves matching class-minimax MSE bounds on \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\). It retains Jin--Mackey--Syrgkanis Theorem 5.4 only as an estimator-specific generalized-quantile upper comparator and treats the bounded-outcome Gaussian calculation solely as a separate source-assumption diagnostic.

related_work: \cite{Robinson1988} supplies the partially linear conditional-mean model, and \cite{ChernozhukovEtAl2018DML} and \cite{NeweyRobins2018} supply orthogonal-score and sample-splitting background. \cite{MackeySyrgkanisZadik2018} gives finite-order orthogonal PLM moments and a Gaussian characterization, not exact all-shift transform annihilation or the present effective fixed-separation minimax theorem. \cite[Theorem 5.4, condition (21), and bound (22)]{JinMackeySyrgkanis2025} is retained exactly on \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\). The proved inclusion \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\subseteq\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\) licenses the full-class spectral upper guarantee, and an ACE-preserving outcome-tilt path gives a class-minimax MSE converse there; neither fact lower-bounds the ACE estimator or converts the cited generalized-quantile comparison into anything other than upper-versus-upper. The simultaneous bounded-outcome Gaussian assumptions stated around that paper's Theorem 3.2 instead force \(\theta_0=0\), so its positive lower-bound claim is not used. \cite{Mattner1992} and \cite{HuShiu2022} inform location-family completeness and observable-zero testing; \cite{DinhGhoshTranTran2021} informs zero localization; \cite{ChackoViceira2003} supplies complex and spectral GMM precedent; \cite{ReizingerEtAl2025} studies linear ICA treatment-effect estimation; and \cite{LeeMesters2024} studies weak-non-Gaussian inference in linear simultaneous equations. None supplies this certified learned-residual PLM contour statistic and fixed-error MSE theorem. These are targeted distinctions, not claims that transform zeros are new, priority claims, or an exhaustive review.
interpretation: The causal target is \(\theta_0(P)\); the observable contour ratio is its identifying functional only on contours satisfying the proved zero-free and positive-count conditions. At fixed separation, certification turns that identity into a computable sample statistic with matched parametric MSE on the broad direct-\(L^1(P_X)\) class. Because the lower-bound outcome tilt also preserves both published \(L^r(P_X)\) code restrictions, the full published ACE class has the same matched minimax MSE order. This is a class-level statement over all estimators, not a lower bound for the particular ACE statistic or its generalized-quantile upper guarantee. The Gaussian bounded-outcome proposition does not establish a Gaussian-versus-non-Gaussian minimax dichotomy: it shows only that one simultaneous source-stated intersection has the identically zero target.
technical_internal_limitation: Constants in the contour-bank and risk bounds may deteriorate as \(\delta\downarrow0\). The current results do not give a sharp phase map in \(n,\varepsilon_{1,n},\varepsilon_{2,n},\delta_n\), a data-driven selector across DML, ACE, and contour regimes, uniformly valid inference, or matching local lower bounds. The ACE comparison is an upper-guarantee comparison, not a lower bound for ACE.
honest_scope: Claim matched fixed-separation \(\Theta(n^{-1})\) MSE on the broad direct-\(L^1(P_X)\) spectral class and on the full published ACE class. On the latter, distinguish the class-minimax lower bound over all estimators from the upper-versus-upper comparison between the cited ACE generalized-quantile guarantee and the spectral guarantee. Retain \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}^{\mathrm{ACE}}\) as the stronger \(L^s(P_X)\) subclass, equal to the published class at \(s=r\). Treat the local-to-Gaussian results as partial upper benchmarks and the bounded-outcome Gaussian calculation solely as an assumption-consistency diagnostic. Do not claim a lower bound for the ACE estimator, novelty of transform zeros or multiplicity-aware methods, adaptive zero estimation, uniform inference, matching local lower bounds, or a Gaussian-versus-non-Gaussian minimax dichotomy.
